Title: 'Not a single minister present': Hassan Karim calls out empty benches
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A government backbencher today expressed disappointment over the absence of ministers in the Dewan Rakyat as he prepared to speak during the policy-stage debate on the Supply Bill 2027.
Hassan Abdul Karim (PH-Pasir Gudang) said he wanted to support Budget 2027, which he believed contained several positive measures, but was disappointed that no minister was present to hear his views.
"Before proceeding with my debate, I would like to express my disappointment that not a single minister is present.
"I am a government backbencher and I want to support this Budget. There are many good things in it, but those most keen to hear what I have to say are my friends in the Opposition.
"But no one from the government is here," he said.
The policy-stage debate on Budget 2027 is scheduled to run until Oct 22, following its tabling by Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on Oct 9.
Ministers are scheduled to deliver their winding-up speeches over four days, starting next week.

Title: MRT Corp and TNB explore green rail solutions, to start with RTS Link
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Rapid Transit Corporation Sdn Bhd (MRT Corp) and Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) will explore renewable energy, energy efficiency and electrical reliability solutions for rail infrastructure.
This will begin with the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link project.
The collaboration will initially focus on the Bukit Chagar Immigration, Customs and Quarantine (ICQ) Complex and Wadi Hana Depot.
The two organisations will assess opportunities to integrate renewable energy, improve energy efficiency and strengthen electrical infrastructure reliability.
The partnership was formalised through a memorandum of understanding (MoU) exchanged at Transport Expo Asia 2026 here today.
The agreement builds on their existing working relationship across the MRT1, MRT2, Penang Mutiara Line and RTS Link projects.
The MoU was exchanged between MRT Corp chief executive officer Datuk Mohd Zarif Hashim and TNB president and chief executive officer Datuk Seri Ir Ts Shamsul Ahmad, witnessed by Transport Minister Loke Siew Fook.
The agreement outlines three areas of collaboration, including solar energy solutions, electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure and electrical reliability and maintenance services.
Under the first area, both parties will explore the development and deployment of renewable energy systems at suitable premises and assets.
This is alongside energy-saving initiatives to reduce electricity consumption and operating costs.
The second area involves potentially introducing EV charging facilities at selected MRT Corp premises.
The organisations will explore how charging infrastructure could complement public transport facilities and encourage more sustainable mobility.
The third area focuses on improving the safety, reliability and operational resilience of electrical systems and generator sets supporting critical rail facilities.
MRT Corp chief executive officer Datuk Mohd Zarif Hashim said the collaboration will support the corporation's transition from infrastructure development towards the efficient and sustainable operation of its assets.
"As MRT Corp takes on the responsibility of operating Wadi Hana Depot, the ICQ Complex and RTS Station at Bukit Chagar, our priorities extend beyond infrastructure delivery to ensuring these facilities are managed efficiently, reliably and sustainably.
"Our longstanding working relationship with TNB has been instrumental in supporting the delivery of our rail projects.
"We are now taking that relationship to a more strategic level, bringing TNB's energy expertise into how we operate and manage these critical facilities.
"This will allow us to explore practical solutions that improve energy efficiency, strengthen operational resilience and ensure our sustainability commitments translate into measurable benefits throughout the operational life of our assets," he said in a statement.
TNB's Shamsul said the collaboration reflected the importance of integrating sustainable energy solutions into the development and operation of critical infrastructure, in line with the National Energy Transition Roadmap (NETR).
"Reliable electricity is fundamental to the effective operation of public transport infrastructure.
"Beyond the initial focus on the RTS Link, the MoU provides a framework for both organisations to explore further opportunities where energy solutions can create value for infrastructure operations," he said.
The partnership aligns with TNB's efforts to advance Malaysia's energy transition through grid modernisation, renewable energy integration and more efficient energy solutions.

Title: Tuition teacher charged with sexual offences against three 11-year-old pupils
Article:
news@nst.com.my
KUALA LUMPUR: A tuition teacher was charged in two Sessions Courts here today with six offences involving sexual assault and unnatural sex against three 11-year-old boys.
However, MD Sebastian, 46, pleaded not guilty to all six charges after they were read out separately before judges Azrul Darus and Ilmami Ahmad.
Four charges alleged that the primary school teacher, who also ran tuition classes, had sexually assaulted the three pupils at a house in Kampung Muhibbah, Jalan Puchong, between July and September.
He was charged under Section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017, which provides for a maximum jail term of 20 years and whipping upon conviction.
He also faced two charges of committing unnatural sex with an 11-year-old pupil at the same location between 5.30pm and 6pm on Sept 18 and 30.
The charges were brought under Section 377C of the Penal Code, which carries a jail term of between five and 20 years, as well as whipping, upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutors V Suloshani and Mohamad Ikhwan Mohd Nasir sought bail of RM10,000 for each charge, with additional conditions that the accused be barred from approaching the victims and prosecution witnesses.
Defence lawyer Mansheel Kaur sought the minimum bail, saying her client had a permanent residence, was not a flight risk and needed to support his ailing parents.
Azrul allowed bail of RM10,000 per case in his court, while Ilmami set bail at RM10,000 per charge, bringing the total bail to RM40,000.
The courts also ordered the accused not to disturb the victims or prosecution witnesses, surrender his passport and report to the police station nearest his residence once a month until the cases are concluded.
The cases were fixed for mention on Nov 23 and Dec 18.
On Oct 16, the teacher was detained to assist investigations into allegations of sexual assault and unnatural sex involving five male students aged between 12 and 16.
He was arrested around 11.30pm on Oct 10 within the compound of the Kuala Lumpur contingent police headquarters before being taken to the Cheras district police headquarters.
Police investigations found that the alleged offences took place at the suspect's house, which also served as a tuition centre.

Title: Greek students, teachers, civil servants plan cost of living protests
Article:
ATHENS: Students, teachers and civil servants will rally in Greece on Wednesday to protest against the high cost of living, saying they face the same problems that sparked violent demonstrations in France at the weekend.
Gatherings are expected around midday (0900 GMT) in Athens and Thessaloniki, the country's second-largest city.
"In Greece like in France, we are demanding public, free education," Katia Koubousidou, head of a student union at the Aristotle University of Thessaloniki, told AFP.
"This will not be a one-off protest. We have a plan to continue our demonstrations."
Dozens of students set up tents in Syntagma Square, facing Parliament, in Athens, and on a pedestrian street in Thessaloniki on Tuesday.
The civil servants' union has also called for a work stoppage and a gathering in Athens.
Secondary school pupils and teachers are protesting about a lack of infrastructure, a shortage of staff and increased public spending on education.
The conservative Greek government has sought in recent days to avoid any parallel with the protests and violence in France.
Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis said on Monday that the country would "never return to the era of great social unrest" during the financial crisis over a decade ago, marked by unpopular austerity measures.
French cities were hit by some of the country's worst rioting in recent years on Saturday, with public buildings torched, hundreds of shops looted and more than 2,000 people arrested.

Title: Court to decide on former judges' pension suit on Jan 28
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court here has fixed Jan 28 next year to deliver its decision on a suit filed by a group of 19 people, comprising former members of the judiciary and widows of former judges, against the government and three others over the alleged failure to provide an appropriate increase in their pensions and benefits since 2015.
Judge S. Indra Nehru fixed the date after hearing submissions by counsel Christopher Leong, representing the plaintiffs, and Senior Federal Counsel Mohammad Sallehuddin Md Ali, who appeared for the defendants.
Earlier, Mohammad Sallehuddin submitted that the originating summons (OS) should be dismissed as the plaintiffs' action had become academic, as there was no longer any actual controversy between the plaintiffs and the defendants that would affect the parties in any way.
Leong countered that the declaration sought could not be considered academic, as it would set a precedent for other retired judges affected by the same issue.
Previously, 36 people, comprising former members of the judiciary and widows of former judges, were named as plaintiffs in the suit filed in Jan 2022.
However, 17 people have been removed as plaintiffs from the suit, including former Chief Judges of Malaya Tan Sri Siti Norma Yaakob, who died in March this year, and Tan Sri Haidar Mohamed Nor, as well as former Court of Appeal judge Tan Sri Mohamad Ariff Md Yusof, who is also a former Dewan Rakyat speaker.
In the suit, retired judges, including former Court of Appeal president Tan Sri Alauddin Mohd Sheriff, named the government, the prime minister, the cabinet and the director-general of public service as the first to fourth defendants.
The plaintiffs seek a declaration that the failure to fix, through a government gazette, an appropriate increment of more than two per cent in their pensions and other benefits pursuant to Section 15B(2) of the Judges' Remuneration Act 1971 had violated Articles 125(7) and 125(9) of the Federal Constitution.
They are also seeking an order that the second or third defendants, namely the prime minister and the cabinet, respectively, advise the Yang di-Pertuan Agong to fix a higher annual increment of more than two per cent in their pensions and other benefits, effective July 1, 2015, pursuant to Section 15B(2) of Act 45.
The plaintiffs also said that, pursuant to Section 15B of the Judges' Remuneration Act 1971, the pensions of retired judges and dependants of deceased judges were adjusted automatically based on the current salaries of serving judges, which were reviewed in stages from time to time, as required under Articles 125(7) and 125(9) of the Federal Constitution.

Title: Video of Kuching international school student's penknife attack goes viral
Article:
KUCHING: A video of an international school student's penknife attack this morning, which left a teacher injured, has gone viral on social media.
Some social media accounts claimed the 16-year-old had livestreamed the attack on an online community platform before the video was deleted.
In the footage, the teen is seen looking at himself in a bathroom mirror with a phone strapped to his head.
He then runs towards a classroom, opens the door and shouts: "This is what you get."
The boy then charges at a
teacher before the screen goes black
. Students can be heard screaming in the background.
Earlier, it was reported that the teacher was injured and taken to hospital. The student was subdued before being taken to the principal's office.
No other injuries have been reported so far.
Police later arrived at the school, while the student's parents were contacted.
Sarawak acting police commissioner Deputy Commissioner Saifullizan Ishak confirmed the incident.
He denied that an axe had been used, although an axe was seen in a separate video near the boy's bag.
As a safety precaution, the school temporarily closed its premises and asked parents to collect their children early.

Title: Civil servant held over RM30mil bribes linked to RM140mil tax assessments
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: A civil servant suspected of soliciting and accepting about RM30 million in bribes to help several companies reduce tax assessments totalling RM140 million was arrested at a hotel in the Klang Valley early today.
The suspect, a man in his 50s who serves as a unit director, was arrested by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) about 12.30am.
He was brought before the Putrajaya Magistrate's Court this morning, where magistrate Ezrene Zakariah granted a six-day remand order until Oct 26.

Title: Gentari, BYD Malaysia explore flash charging rollout
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Gentari Sdn Bhd and BYD Malaysia Sdn Bhd are exploring the deployment of BYD Flash Charging technology as the country's electric vehicle (EV) market continues to expand.
Both companies signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to explore this prospect today.
The collaboration will assess opportunities to develop high-power charging infrastructure supported by battery energy storage systems (BESS), with the technology capable of delivering about 400 kilometres of driving range in as little as five minutes for compatible vehicles under optimal conditions.
Under the MoU, the companies will identify suitable charging locations, including key intercity corridors connecting major population centres.
They will also evaluate power infrastructure requirements, technical and commercial feasibility, project development opportunities and potential operating models.
The partnership will also explore opportunities in renewable energy generation and energy storage, combining Gentari's clean energy expertise with BYD's energy storage and technology capabilities.
Malaysia recorded 53,537 new EV registrations in the first nine months of 2026, an increase of 98.8 per cent from the corresponding period last year.
The growth comes as the government works towards establishing 30,000 public EV charging points nationwide by 2030.
Gentari, the clean energy solutions company wholly owned by Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas), currently operates more than 600 EV charging points in Malaysia.
It provides access to about 18,000 charging points across Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and India through its Gentari Go Roaming Hub.
Gentari group chief executive officer Sushil Purohit said the next phase of EV adoption will depend on the quality, convenience and reliability of charging services, beyond charging speed alone.
He said BYD's expertise in EVs, batteries and high-power charging technology, combined with Gentari's experience in developing and operating charging networks, will provide a foundation for strengthening Malaysia's EV charging ecosystem.
BYD vice-president and Asia Pacific auto sales division general manager Liu Xueliang said Malaysia was an important market for the company as it expanded its advanced charging technology into international markets.
He said the collaboration would explore how BYD Flash Charging could support a faster and more convenient charging experience for Malaysian EV users.
BYD Malaysia managing director Jacob Ma said the partnership was an important step towards building a more comprehensive EV ecosystem in the country.
He added that a seamless ownership experience is essential to encouraging more consumers to switch to electric vehicles.
The MoU was signed by Purohit and Ma in Shenzhen, Guangdong, China, on Wednesday.
Representatives from both organisations, including Petronas and Gentari executives, as well as BYD Group chairman Wang Chuanfu were present.

Title: 'As a grandfather, I feel their pain': Zahid mourns five-year-old Asiah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said he was deeply moved by the death of 5-year-old Asiah Ahmad Syahir in a six-vehicle crash on Jalan Kuching, particularly as he has grandchildren of the same age.
Zahid, who visited the girl's family in Kampung Sungai Penchala earlier today, said it was heartbreaking to see a young life cut short.
"As a grandfather with grandchildren of the same age, I was deeply moved by the loss of a little girl who should have had so much of her life ahead of her.
"It is difficult to imagine the depth of a family's grief when a little child who once brought joy to their home is suddenly no longer with them," he said in a Facebook post.
Zahid expressed his condolences and prayed for the family to remain strong.
He also reminded motorists that a moment of carelessness on the road could have devastating consequences.
"Every decision we make on the road carries responsibility, because a single act of negligence can leave a lasting scar on the lives of others and their families," he said.
Asiah died from severe head injuries following the
crash on Oct 10
while travelling with her family along Jalan Kuching towards Segambut.
On Thursday,
Raeven Goh Wey Haur
, 24, claimed trial at the magistrate's court here to three charges, including dangerous driving causing Asiah's death.

Title: JP Morgan sees Bank Negara rate hike in Q1 2027
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bank Negara Malaysia is expected to raise the overnight policy rate (OPR) by 25 basis points (bps) in the first quarter of 2027, according to JP Morgan.
The US investment bank said it expects Bank Negara to keep the benchmark rate unchanged at its upcoming November policy meeting before raising it by 25bps in Q1 2027.
The forecast suggests Bank Negara could begin tightening monetary policy next year as strong growth momentum supports the outlook for domestic economic activity.
A rate increase will mark a shift towards tighter monetary conditions, potentially raising borrowing costs for households and businesses while supporting efforts to keep inflationary pressures in check.
On inflation, JP Morgan kept its headline and core consumer price index (CPI) forecasts at 1.8 per cent and 1.9 per cent respectively for this year, with both gauges stepping down to 1.7 per cent next year.
"But as we have previously highlighted, elevated and still-rising input costs point to upside inflation risks," it added.
In contrast to most regional peers, JP Morgan said inflation in Malaysia has remained rangebound at between 1.8 per cent and 2.0 per cent over the past six months.
This is despite elevated energy prices, helped by subsidies for fuel and electricity as well as still-benign core price pressures.
Following a slight uptick to 1.9 per cent in August, headline inflation ticked back down to 1.8 per cent last month, printing below expectations.
Notwithstanding the cushion from petrol and diesel subsidies, the firm said the transport fuel CPI gained another 1.4 per cent month-on-month in September.
However, this was more than fully offset by a larger-than-expected 3.1 per cent drop in electricity prices.
"The larger drop in electricity prices than implied by the automatic fuel adjustment rate set in September owes to expanded electricity subsidies which now protect users consuming up to 800 kilowatt-hour (kWh) electricity per month, up from 600kWh earlier.
"As of now, this threshold is set to revert to 600kWh in January 2027," JP Morgan said.

Title: Sultan of Pahang warns youths against social ills, culture of hatred
Article:
PEKAN: The Sultan of Pahang has expressed concern over worsening social ills among youths, including drug abuse, bullying, online gambling and inappropriate relationships.
Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri'ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah said it was saddening that some youths were easily influenced by a culture of hatred towards religion and institutions, as if courage were measured by how loudly they insulted and belittled others.
He stressed that university students should be voices of wisdom, not echoes of hatred.
"Be brave enough to speak up, but do so with courtesy. Be brave enough to disagree, but never lose your sense of judgement," he said in his speech at the proclamation ceremony for Universiti Malaysia Pahang Al-Sultan Abdullah's (UMPSA) Tuanku Chancellor Hall here today.
Also present were Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir, Pahang Education Committee chairman Datuk Seri Ir Mohd Soffi Abd Razak and UMPSA Pro-Chancellor Tan Sri Abi Musa Asa'ari Mohamed Nor.
On education, Al-Sultan Abdullah said he did not want the pursuit of a degree to overshadow the true purpose of acquiring knowledge.
He said artificial intelligence (AI) should be used to enhance critical thinking rather than become a shortcut that discouraged students from thinking, researching and innovating.
"Let us not produce a generation rich in certificates but poor in knowledge, eloquent in speech but lacking in thought," he said.
Meanwhile, he called on UMPSA to strengthen collaboration with the state government, industry players, foundations and alumni to expand educational assistance, research and local talent development.
Al-Sultan Abdullah said the university's expertise in technology, manufacturing, automotive, logistics and modern agriculture should be translated into tangible benefits for the people.
"Let the knowledge acquired here reach rural communities, stimulate the economy and improve people's lives," he said.
Meanwhile, the ruler commended the efforts of UMPSA and the Pahang Islamic Religious and Malay Customs Council in developing Kolej Kediaman Mawaddah, a residential college established through waqf (Islamic charitable endowment).
"Such initiatives should be expanded. I urge the Federal Government, particularly the Higher Education Ministry, to give due attention to developing residential colleges, faculties and supporting facilities at UMPSA," he said.

Title: Akmal to auction motorcycle, tilapia to pay RM300,000 to Teresa Kok
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh is auctioning his Honda X-ADV motorcycle and farmed tilapia to raise RM300,000 to pay DAP veteran Teresa Kok after losing a defamation suit against her.
In a Facebook post, he said he had decided to sell the two assets after realising his savings were insufficient to cover the amount ordered by the court.
He said he appreciated suggestions from friends and supporters to set up a donation fund to help him pay the sum, but wanted to try raising the money himself first.
"I know every friend has a family, responsibilities and their own difficulties. As long as I still have my own assets that I can sell, let me try to raise the money myself first," he said.
Akmal said he respected the court's decision and was prepared to take responsibility for paying the RM300,000.
He said the Honda X-ADV and his farmed tilapia were the only two assets he had fully paid for and could sell, adding that he did not own land or a house that could be sold to raise the money.
He said serious bidders would have to pay a RM100 deposit and submit the payment receipt, along with details of the asset they wished to bid for and their offered price.
The deposit would be refunded in full if the bid was unsuccessful, he added.
Akmal said parting with the two assets would be difficult because they held sentimental value for him.
"It is difficult to part with something we love. However, it is harder for me to burden others when I still have my own assets that I can sell," he said.
He also thanked those who had offered prayers and words of encouragement, saying their support already meant a great deal to him.
"Do not feel guilty if you cannot buy or help. Your prayers and words of encouragement already mean so much to me," he said.
He also asked his supporters to pray for him to have the strength to part with the assets and fulfil his responsibility.
On Monday,
the Melaka High Court
ruled in favour of Kok in her defamation suit against Akmal, ordering him to pay RM250,000 in general and aggravated damages, along with RM50,000 in costs.
The suit concerned remarks Akmal made about Kok in a TikTok video in September 2024, following her criticism of a proposal to make halal certification mandatory for eateries that do not serve pork or alcohol.
The court also ordered Akmal to remove the video from his social media accounts within seven days and barred him from publishing or broadcasting the defamatory statements, or words to the same effect.

Title: Penang named Southeast Asia's only city on National Geographic's 2027 travel list
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Penang has been named the only destination in Southeast Asia featured in National Geographic's The Best Places in the World to Travel to in 2027, earning international recognition for its heritage, culture and natural attractions.
State Tourism and Creative Economy Committee chairman Wong Hon Wai said the list, unveiled yesterday, featured 25 destinations and travel experiences recommended for travellers next year.
"Penang is proud to be among the destinations featured in this prestigious annual list, which offers travellers inspiration and compelling reasons to explore the world in the coming year," he said.
Wong said Penang's selection followed a nomination, research and reporting process involving National Geographic's travel experts and Nat Geo Traveler's international editorial teams.
The publication highlighted Penang's distinctive geographical and cultural character, shaped by the relationship between Penang Island and mainland Seberang Perai.
It described the destination as offering a mix of Unesco-protected streets in George Town, rainforest-fringed beaches, traditional kampongs and mangrove-filled rivers, alongside the mainland's modern industrial hubs.
Wong said the recognition reflected Penang's diverse attractions and its ability to offer visitors a combination of heritage, nature, culture and contemporary experiences.
"Being featured once again by National Geographic further reinforces Penang's appeal as an international tourism destination.
"It reflects the island's distinctive character and the experiences that continue to make it attractive to visitors from around the world," he said.
He noted that Penang had also received National Geographic recognition in 2025 for its food, highlighting the state's celebrated culinary heritage.
Wong said the latest inclusion could raise Penang's international profile, strengthen its appeal to overseas travellers and increase awareness of the state as a tourism destination.
He credited the recognition to the collective efforts of tourism operators, industry stakeholders and organisations involved in developing and promoting Penang.
"More importantly, this international recognition is a testament to the dedication, close collaboration and sustained efforts of Penang's tourism industry stakeholders, who have worked tirelessly to develop and promote our destination," he said.
Wong stressed that the achievement belonged to the wider tourism industry rather than any single organisation, reflecting continued collaboration to strengthen the state's tourism sector.
"This honour belongs to all our tourism industry stakeholders. Their collective commitment, collaboration and perseverance have contributed to Penang's continued development as a tourism destination," he added.
He said the state government would continue to enhance its tourism offerings, strengthen Penang's branding and expand its reach in international markets.
"We will continue to enhance Penang's tourism brand, raise its international profile and strengthen its appeal, with the aim of welcoming more international visitors to experience all that Penang has to offer," he said.
National Geographic's 2027 list features destinations around the world, including Vestland in Norway, Luxor in Egypt, Niigata in Japan, Chengdu in China, Jaipur in India, Melbourne in Australia and Malawi.
Penang's inclusion places the Malaysian destination among a diverse selection of locations recognised for their distinctive attractions and travel experiences.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: For Lula, Brazil's sovereignty is at stake in final election
Article:
WHEN Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva addressed the United Nations General Assembly last month, he used one of the world's biggest diplomatic stages to deliver a message that has come to define what is likely the final presidential campaign of his decades-long career.
"Brazil does not fit into anyone's backyard," he said, in a veiled dig at US President Donald Trump's administration, which he believes is challenging Brazil's sovereignty.
Lula has portrayed Brazil's election as part of a wider battle against undemocratic forces, warning of "foreign interference" in a race that concludes on Sunday in a heated runoff against right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro.
In the candidates' first debate days before the vote, Lula accused the Bolsonaro family, headed by former President Jair Bolsonaro, of being "subordinate to American interests," pointing to May meetings between the Bolsonaros and Trump earlier this year before Trump imposed new tariffs on Brazilian products.
In July, Lula said the new tariffs were the result of a "plot" with the Bolsonaros "driven by electoral objectives."
Last year, the senator's brother Eduardo Bolsonaro, who lives in the US, described Trump's tariffs on Brazilian beef, coffee, fish, footwear and other goods as "bitter medicine" aimed at curbing what he called an out-of-check legal offensive against his father.
"The pressure they applied to get the United States to put tariffs on Brazil, and their appeal for Brazil to suffer some harm," Lula said at the debate.
"The brother is over there inciting a coup against Brazil."
The family denied the accusations. The State Department has also denied previous accusations of election interference.
The election's first round showed the limits to Lula's message.
[[nid:1560646]]
Over 47 per cent of voters backed Bolsonaro, an outspoken Trump ally, nearly two percentage points ahead of Lula.
Lula enters the final days trailing slightly in the polls to Bolsonaro, whose father is serving a 27-year sentence for plotting a failed coup against Lula's electoral win in 2022.
Although Lula enters the election as the underdog, he is confident he can stage a dramatic comeback.
He has done so before. After spending 580 days in prison in 2018 and 2019 on a corruption conviction that was later overturned, he narrowly defeated Jair Bolsonaro in 2022.
"As long as I am alive, the far right will not return to power in this country," he has said on the campaign trail.
Lula and his allies continue to fight what they see as international interference to keep him from a fourth term.
His campaign accused US tech giant Meta, which owns Instagram, WhatsApp and Facebook, of manipulating social media days before the vote.
Meta blamed global technical glitches and denied political bias.
Lula has portrayed his opponent as a stand-in for a broader right-wing movement, sharing images linking him to Trump, Argentina's President Javier Milei and Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
With right-wing parties sweeping recent elections across Latin America, Lula and his allies see Sunday's runoff as a chance to stem the region's conservative drift.
"Lula is a symbol of the fight against Trump's imperialism ... of the liberation of Latin America and the world," Paulo Saboia, a 67-year-old retired IT technician, said at a Lula rally in Sao Paulo.
* The writers are from Reuters

Title: Nancy: Counselling for victims of AI-generated nude images
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The Women, Family and Community Development Ministry is offering counselling to victims of AI-generated nude images and their families following a case involving female students in Negri Sembilan.
Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said the service was also available to parents who needed support to cope with the emotional distress caused by the incident.
She said the ministry had counsellors through its agencies, including the Social Welfare Department and the National Population and Family Development Board, who could assist victims and their families.
"We want to inform families that if they need counselling, our ministry can help," she told reporters after officiating the 2026 National Breast Cancer Awareness Month celebration at the Waterfront Convention Centre Penang (PWCC).
On Oct 18, media reports said more than
300 female secondary school students
in Seremban, Negri Sembilan, were believed to have been victims of AI-powered image manipulation to create nude images.
The compromising images were reportedly circulated among students at the school and allegedly sold through the Telegram messaging application.
The case has raised concerns over the misuse of AI to create fake images that could humiliate victims and undermine their emotional well-being.

Title: Perhilitan action in Chemor prompts elephants to move away
Article:
IPOH: The Wildlife and National Parks Department (Perhilitan) has driven wild elephants away from Bukit Bangkong, Chemor, following repeated incursions into orchards.
In a statement, Perhilitan said it received complaints about elephant disturbances on Sept 27, Oct 3 and Oct 11.
The department began monitoring the area on Oct 4 before carrying out control measures on the nights of Oct 11 and 12.
"Field observations found that the herd had moved away from the reported area following the control measures," it said.
Further measures were carried out from Oct 16 to 17 to address recurring disturbances and reduce the risk of human-elephant conflict.
Perhilitan also advised residents and plantation owners to install lights around plantations and use bonfires in a controlled manner to reduce the likelihood of further incursions.
"Residents and plantation owners are also urged to immediately notify the department if the disturbances recur to enable prompt follow-up action," the statement said.
The department said it would continue to monitor the area and take further action if necessary.
On Oct 16, the New Straits Times reported that
wild elephants had raided fruit
orchards in Bukit Bangkong three times within weeks, damaging fruit trees, water tanks, pipes and ponds.
The Bukit Bangkong Hulu Cemor farmers' group said the repeated incursions had raised concerns among orchard owners who had invested considerable time, effort and money in developing their land.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: #NSTViral: Police hunt Porsche driver over road bullying in Bandar Kinrara
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police are tracking down the driver of a black Porsche Cayenne caught on dashcam footage driving recklessly, chasing another motorist and attempting to force the vehicle to stop in Bandar Kinrara.
The incident occurred near a Shell petrol station in Bandar Kinrara 3 on Sunday and has since gone viral on social media, drawing concern over the driver's behaviour.
Federal Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department (TEID) director Datuk Seri Mohammed Hasbullah Ali said police had opened an investigation after footage of the incident was shared on the Dashcam Owners Malaysia Facebook page.
The post, titled "The infamous Porsche Cayenne in Puchong & Kinrara", featured several photographs and dashcam recordings of the black SUV.
It also warned other motorists to exercise caution if they encountered the vehicle.
Hasbullah said initial investigations found that the incident occurred around 2.15pm on Oct 18 along a three-lane road near Bandar Kinrara 3.
"The car with the dashcam was travelling from Puchong towards Bukit Jalil in the leftmost lane when the Porsche Cayenne attempted to change lanes without signalling.
"The driver sounded the horn after noticing the Porsche attempting to move into the lane without indicating.
"The driver then accelerated, prompting the Porsche driver to give chase," he said.
Hasbullah said the situation escalated when the Porsche driver allegedly applied the brakes in an attempt to force the other vehicle to stop.
The Porsche was also seen obstructing the other motorist's path, he added.
Police are working to identify the Porsche driver and locate witnesses who may have seen the incident.
Investigators are also examining available closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage and dashcam recordings to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident.
Hasbullah said police had received a report from the dashcam vehicle's driver on Oct 18 and he would be called in to have his statement recorded.
A separate police report concerning the viral video was lodged by a traffic investigating officer from the Serdang district police headquarters at 9.58pm on Oct 19.
Checks revealed that the Porsche Cayenne was registered to a company, while the identity of the person driving it at the time of the incident has yet to be established.
The case is being investigated under Section 42(1) of the Road Transport Act for reckless and dangerous driving.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Complex chip development can cost up to US$300 million
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Developing complex semiconductor chips can cost up to US$300 million, posing a major challenge for local companies seeking to venture into the industry's upstream segment.
Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said the high costs meant companies needed substantial capital to develop chips tailored to their technologies and requirements.
He said the government's collaboration with global technology company ARM provided access to technology but did not cover the full cost of chip development.
"Even a simple chip costs about US$50 million, while a complex chip can cost up to US$300 million," he said in the Dewan Rakyat.
He was responding to a question from Datuk Ku Abd Rahman Ku Ismail (Bersatu-Kubang Pasu).
Johari said the collaboration with ARM, signed in 2025, provides two types of tokens — Compute Subsystem (CSS) and ARM Flexible Access (AFA) — to help local companies develop integrated circuit chip designs.
He said access to the technology could shorten development time by up to two years, accelerating efforts by companies to develop their own intellectual property.
"Of the seven CSS tokens, we have only provided four so far," he said.
Johari said the tokens provided were estimated to be worth between RM30 million and RM40 million, but companies still needed additional funding to complete chip development.
The development process is expected to take between two and two-and-a-half years, depending on the technology used.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Australian lawmaker loses both legs, knew family of suspected attacker
Article:
MELBOURNE: Australian lawmaker Helen Haines has had both legs removed, her husband told journalists on Wednesday, after what police called a "targeted" attack.
Haines is in a stable condition at a Melbourne hospital after being struck by a car on Monday near her office in the town of Wangaratta, more than 200 kilometres northeast of the Victoria state capital.
Speaking at the hospital on Wednesday, her husband Phil said that surgeons had been forced to remove both her legs.
"But the good news in all this is Helen is alive and she's stable. That is the most important thing for our family," he said.
"The two most important parts of Helen for us as a family are her heart and her mind," he said.
"Her heart is huge. She is a very compassionate, caring, loving person."
The man alleged to have wounded Haines, in what police have called a "targeted" attack, faced court earlier on Wednesday.
Police have charged 43-year-old Brendan Nugent with dangerous driving causing serious injury and intentionally causing serious injury, as well as the federal crime of harming a public official, which carries a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison.
He has also been charged with cultivating a cannabis plant and possession of the drug, according to court documents
In another report, the family of Nugent, had been friends with her for more than 20 years, according to
ABC
on Wednesday, citing the suspect's relatives, reported Sputnik/RIA Novosti.
"Helen has been our friend for more than 20 years and what happened to her yesterday is devastating and unfathomable," Nugent's father, Rod Nugent, told
ABC
.
The accused's relatives described Haines as a deeply respected and beloved member of the local community and expressed their support for her family.
According to investigators, Brendan Nugent intentionally struck Haines twice with a Toyota Land Cruiser SUV near her parliamentary office in Wangaratta, Victoria, on Monday afternoon.
The suspect defence lawyer said Nugent suffers from a rare neurological condition, idiopathic transverse myelitis, which affects the spinal cord, and had also sustained a concussion.
Nugent has been charged with dangerous driving, intentionally causing serious injury, and causing harm to a federal public official.
The judge ordered Nugent to undergo a medical examination.
He is not seeking bail and will remain in custody until his next hearing on Feb 4, 2027.
The motive for the attack has not been established.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Two hikers swept away by strong currents at Batang Kali waterfall
Article:
BATANG KALI: A search and rescue operation is underway for two hikers swept away by strong currents while swimming at Lubuk Tupai Waterfall in Kampung Hulu Rening.
The two were part of a group of six who had gone hiking in the area.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department received a distress call at 12.13pm.
Two of the hikers had entered the river for a swim but were swept away by strong currents and disappeared underwater, he said.
Ashrul said rescue personnel faced difficulties reaching the waterfall due to its remote location.
"Firefighters had to trek between four and five kilometres uphill from the base camp in Kampung Hulu Rening to reach the scene.
"Personnel from the Batang Kali Volunteer Fire Brigade arrived at the waterfall at 1.05pm, while firefighters from the Kuala Kubu Bharu Fire and Rescue Station reached the location at 2.28pm," he said.
He said rescuers were conducting an initial assessment of the area before proceeding with rescue efforts.
A total of 10 personnel from the Kuala Kubu Bharu Fire and Rescue Station and Batang Kali Volunteer Fire Brigade were involved in the operation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Injured teacher rushed to hospital after wresting penknife from student
Article:
KUCHING: A teacher was injured while trying to wrest a sharp object from a student at an international school here this morning.
In a notice to parents, guardians, staff and students, the school said the incident was isolated and no other injuries were reported.
The student was subdued before being taken to the principal's office and placed under supervision.
Police arrived shortly after and contacted the student's parents.
The injured teacher received treatment after the school called an ambulance before being taken to hospital.
All students were immediately evacuated to ensure their safety.
The school said the student had not approached other students and that no students were in danger throughout the incident.
It reaffirmed its commitment to the safety of students and staff, as well as open communication to ensure the school community received accurate information.
Sarawak acting police commissioner Deputy Commissioner Saifullizan Ishak confirmed the incident in a statement, saying a penknife, rather than an axe, was involved, Dayak Daily reported.
He issued the clarification following the circulation of a viral video allegedly of the incident, in which an axe was seen.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia condemns Houthi attacks, stresses safe passage through Strait of Hormuz
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has condemned Houthi attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure in Saudi Arabia and other Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said Malaysia continued to view with great concern the escalation of conflict unfolding across the Middle East.
"We remain steadfast in our call for peace and justice for the Palestinian people, in our unequivocal condemnation of the genocide in Gaza, and in our opposition to the indiscriminate bombing of southern Lebanon.
"That same conviction obliges us to speak with equal clarity and firmness when civilians are attacked elsewhere.
"Malaysia reiterates its condemnation of the attacks by the Houthis on civilians and civilian infrastructure, including airports and oil and energy installations, whether in Saudi Arabia or in any other GCC state," he said in a statement.
Anwar cited the recent attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, which he said killed civilians, including pilgrims.
On Oct 10, a Houthi missile struck the airport, killing at least 13 people and wounding more than 300, in the
deadliest attack
on Saudi Arabia in more than a decade.
In the weeks before and after the Oct 10 attack, the Houthis launched at least 10 other attacks targeting five Saudi airports.
A subsequent strike on the airport in Riyadh on Oct 11 killed another person, bringing the total death toll from the airport attacks to at least 20.
"It is a sad reminder of what such violence costs ordinary people," Anwar said.
He said he had been in close contact with regional leaders, including Saudi Crown Prince Mohamed Salman and Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed Abdulrahman Al Thani, as well as other Gulf leaders.
"These conversations reflect the gravity with which Malaysia regards the present crisis, and the urgency of preventing it from spreading further," he said.
He said Malaysia's concern was with those responsible, not with Yemenis.
"Our concern lies with those responsible for these attacks, not with the Yemeni people, who have endured years of conflict and deserve a lasting political settlement."
Anwar also highlighted the importance of Middle Eastern sea lanes to Malaysia.
"The security of the Middle East's sea lanes is paramount.
"As a trading nation, Malaysia's prosperity rests upon open and secure maritime routes," he said.
He said he had repeatedly underlined the need for the safe passage of civilian and commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.
"Malaysia will continue to support diplomatic efforts to de-escalate the crisis and safeguard freedom of navigation," he said.
The Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia came after the group announced in July that it would target Saudi shipping in the Red Sea and infrastructure inside the kingdom, following a Saudi attack on the Houthi-controlled airport in Sanaa.
Malaysia Airlines
cancelled
all flights connecting Kuala Lumpur (KUL) and Johor Bahru (JHB) with Jeddah (JED) and Madinah (MED) from Oct 12 to 17 due to security concerns following the airport attacks in Saudi Arabia. Normal operations resumed on Oct 18.
The Houthis said the strikes were in response to an intensified Saudi air campaign in Yemen, and renewed warnings to international airlines against flying to Saudi airports.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Agent charged with harbouring 7 undocumented migrants, possessing 6 passports
Article:
PASIR MAS: An agent was charged at the Sessions Court here today with harbouring seven undocumented migrants and possessing six passports belonging to other people without lawful authority in Tumpat on Oct 14.
Chua Kee Lin, 40, pleaded not guilty to both charges before judge Zulkpli Abdullah.
He was charged with harbouring seven Indonesian migrants by allowing them to remain in a Nissan Serena at a road junction near Kampung Pauh Ganja, Pasir Pekan, Tumpat, at 8.25am on Oct 14.
The charge was framed under Section 55E(1) of the Immigration Act 1959/63.
Chua also claimed trial to possessing six passports belonging to other people without lawful authority at Kampung Kok Seraya, Tumpat, at 9.05am on the same day.
He was charged under Section 12(1)(f) of the Passport Act 1966.
Under Section 55E(2) of the Immigration Act 1959/63, the offence carries a fine of between RM5,000 and RM30,000, or jail for up to 12 months, or both, for each undocumented migrant found on the premises.
For a subsequent conviction, the penalty is a fine of between RM10,000 and RM60,000, or jail for up to two years, or both, for each undocumented migrant.
Under Section 12(1) of the Passport Act 1966, the offence carries a maximum fine of RM10,000, jail for up to five years, or both.
Chua was represented by lawyer Lim Kwang Ching of KC Lim & Partners, while Siti Khaidijah Khairuddin prosecuted.
The court granted him bail of RM10,000 for the charge under the Immigration Act and RM15,000 for the passport charge, bringing his total bail to RM25,000.
The court fixed Nov 22 for mention and submission of documents.
In a separate case at the same court, the seven Indonesian women pleaded guilty to overstaying in Malaysia under Section 15(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63.
The women, aged between 20 and 51, were each fined RM10,000, in default two months' imprisonment.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump says companies should pay 'dividend' to communities to make data centres popular
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that companies building data centres should pay a "dividend" to the communities where they are sited if they want to make the developments popular.
"I have watched the process closely, and data centres that were highly unpopular in a certain area, have become extremely popular when a financial deal is struck," Trump said in a Truth Social post.
Data centres fuelling the rise of AI have become a political flashpoint in communities across the country given the high quantities of water and power they require, with opposition uniting voters across ideological lines.
The Trump administration, which has prioritised rapid AI development to compete with China, has also noted the shifting voter sentiment.
"New and large, in some cases gigantic, Data (centres) are mandated by me to make their own electricity, and give or sell any excess back to the local community, or grid," Trump said in his post.
Trump said in February that major technology companies must build their own power plants for their data centres in order to protect consumers from rising bills.
AI giant Anthropic and Elon Musk have laid out blueprints in recent days for sharing some of the spoils of the AI boom.
The creator of Claude models said over the weekend it is committing five per cent of its shares to a new fund for the "public good", while Musk pledged on Monday to give one SpaceX share to "every kid in America", arguing for such direct distributions as the burgeoning sector faces public scrutiny.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Timeline: Pas and Bersatu in Perlis political crisis
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Political turmoil in Perlis has resurfaced following Bersatu's decision to suspend Menteri Besar Abu Bakar Hamzah.
The latest development comes less than a year after a leadership crisis saw Pas lose the Menteri Besar's post to Bersatu.
Here is a timeline of key developments in the Perlis political crisis.
Nov 2022: Perikatan Nasional (PN) wins 14 of Perlis' 15 state seats, with nine held by Pas and five by Bersatu.
Mid-Dec 2025: Five Bersatu and three Pas assemblymen reportedly withdraw support for Menteri Besar Mohd Shukri Ramli.
Dec 22, 2025: Mohd Shukri is hospitalised amid the political crisis.
Dec 24, 2025: Pas terminates the membership of three assemblymen involved in withdrawing support for Mohd Shukri.
Dec 25, 2025: Mohd Shukri resigns as Menteri Besar, citing health reasons.
Dec 28, 2025: Bersatu's Abu Bakar Hamzah is sworn in as the new Menteri Besar.
Dec 31, 2025: Three Perlis state seats are declared vacant, leaving Pas with six seats and Bersatu with five.
July: Abu Bakar resigns from Bersatu's supreme council but remains a party member and Menteri Besar.
September: Abu Bakar calls for stronger cooperation among PN component parties and urges Perlis Bersatu chairman Izizam Ibrahim to resolve internal party disputes.
Oct 13: Bersatu suspends Abu Bakar's membership rights for two party election terms.
Oct 20: The Registrar of Societies cancels PN's registration.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man charged with raping 15-year-old girl in Rompin
Article:
KUANTAN: A 20-year-old man claimed trial at the Sessions Court here today to raping a 15-year-old girl in a hotel in Rompin in June.
Sarih Naqiuden Sarih Md Sukri entered the plea after the charge was read to him by a court interpreter before judge Sazlina Safie.
According to the charge, he was accused of raping the girl in a hotel room in Rompin between 6pm on June 23 and 5am the following day.
The charge was framed under Section 376(1) of the Penal Code, which provides for a jail term of up to 20 years and whipping upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Fatin Nadirah Kasim prosecuted, while the accused was represented by lawyer Mohd Fadzli Mohd Ramly.
Fatin proposed bail of RM12,000 with one surety, with conditions that the accused refrain from contacting or disturbing the victim and report to the nearest police station.
In mitigation, Fadzli sought a lower bail amount, saying the proposed sum was too high as his client worked in the village and earned RM1,000 a month.
Sazlina set bail at RM5,000 with one surety. She also ordered the accused to report to the Rompin district police headquarters once a month until the case concludes, refrain from disturbing the victim and witnesses, and surrender his passport to the court.
The court fixed Nov 17 for mention.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: North Korea says 'new firepower units' in place after border threat
Article:
SEOUL: North Korea has moved new units into "firing positions", the powerful sister of leader Kim Jong Un said Wednesday, days after Pyongyang warned it was considering deploying additional strike means to its border with South Korea.
Tensions between Seoul and Pyongyang have soared since the South last month blamed an explosion inside the heavily fortified Demilitarised Zone (DMZ) separating the two countries on landmines laid by North Korea, an accusation it has rejected.
"Our military leadership underlined the need to make those rogues aware that our new firepower units have taken their firing positions," Kim Yo Jong said, according to state media.
Her statement came a day after Seoul warned of a "firm" response to further North Korean provocations.
She added that Kim Jong Un had "issued an order to fortify the border with an enemy state to be eternally impregnable."
The statement came as the Korea Central News Agency said the armed forces' Marshal Pak Jong Chon had inspected "pivotal positions" on the border, stressing to troops it was "time to organise the firepower strong enough to strike terror into the enemy's heart."
"If the enemy troops make a provocation actually threatening the safety of our service personnel... The border forces of the DPRK must take very proficient, specialised and overwhelming military action," he said, using the acronym for the North's official name.
Seoul's military accused Pyongyang on Tuesday of attempting to shift the blame for escalating military tensions, while confirming it had used both loudspeakers and warning shots as "legitimate defensive measures to prevent North Korean troops from crossing the MDL (Military Demarcation Line) and to drive back troops that have crossed it."
Jin Yong-sung, chairman of South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff, ordered the military to "respond with firm resolve" should North Korea use Seoul's actions as a pretext for aggressive action, while the defence ministry warned they would be met with "resolute" punishment.
North Korea has separately tested a slew of weapons recently, including a "new-type" precision-guided torpedo system and an intermediate-range hypersonic missile, both of which were said to employ AI technology.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Lecturer loses RM270,000 to phone scam, duped into handing over ATM card
Article:
KUANTAN: A lecturer lost RM269,993 after falling victim to a phone scam in which she was tricked into surrendering her bank card and pawning her jewellery.
The 49-year-old woman was threatened with an arrest warrant and imprisonment over an alleged money-laundering offence, prompting her to make payments purportedly for bail.
Pahang acting police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the victim's ordeal began on April 20 when she received a call at her workplace from a man claiming to be an officer from the National Financial Crime Centre (NFCC).
"The caller claimed the victim's personal information had been misused and linked to an alleged World Coin Trading investment scam. The call was then transferred to a police officer, who claimed she was involved in a money-laundering case.
"She was threatened with an arrest warrant, the freezing of her bank accounts and imprisonment before being instructed to surrender her automated teller machine (ATM) card and make payments purportedly for bail," he said in a statement today.
Azry said the victim, who did not have sufficient cash, borrowed from several people and pawned her jewellery before being instructed to hand over her ATM card at a location specified by the suspects.
"The victim transferred RM43,000 to six different bank accounts between Aug 29 and Sept 13, as instructed by the suspects. Upon checking her bank statement, she discovered seven other transactions involving transfers totalling RM226,993 to five different accounts.
"She realised she had been cheated and lodged a police report yesterday. Her ATM card remains in the suspects' possession," he said.
Azry said the case was being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code for cheating.
He advised the public not to surrender their ATM cards, personal identification numbers or banking details, or make payments in response to instructions received through suspicious phone calls.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NCT Alliance earns Selangor industrial park recognition
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: NCT Alliance Bhd has received the Preferred Industrial Park (PIP) certificate from Invest Selangor, recognising its role in supporting the state's industrial development through its flagship NCT Smart Industrial Park (NSIP).
NCT Alliance said the recognition reinforces its commitment to developing quality industrial parks and attracting high-impact investments to Selangor.
The certificate was presented during the Selangor International Business Summit (SIBS) 2026.
NCT Alliance executive chairman and group managing director Datuk Seri Yap Ngan Choy said the certification reflected the company's strong partnership with Invest Selangor and its commitment to meeting the evolving needs of investors and businesses.
"We look forward to building on this partnership to attract more investments, forge stronger industry connections and contribute to the continued growth of South Selangor as a key economic growth corridor," said Yap.
Spanning about 910 acres, NSIP has a gross development value (GDV) of RM10.2 billion and is positioned as Malaysia's largest GreenRE-certified environmental, social and governance (ESG) managed industrial park.
The development incorporates artificial intelligence, Internet of Things technology, data analytics and automation, alongside smart and sustainable solutions under its managed industrial park model.
NCT Alliance said the country's first Managed Industrial Park (MIP) recently completed the vacant possession handover for Phase 1.
This was followed by the launch of KM2 in Phase 2, which is targeted for completion in 2029.
The company is also planning to launch the Smart Commercial Hub within NSIP in early 2027, with registrations expected to begin in the fourth quarter of 2026.
At SIBS 2026, NCT Alliance also showcased its second industrial park development, NCT Innosphere (NIS).
NIS is located on 55.44 hectares of free-zone land within the Delapan Special Border Economic Zone in Bukit Kayu Hitam, Kedah.
Developed in partnership with Northern Gateway Group, a wholly owned subsidiary of the Minister of Finance Inc, NIS has an estimated GDV of RM1.10 billion and has secured provisional Silver GreenRE certification.
The development comprises eight phases offering 230 industrial units, including terrace, cluster, semi-detached and detached factories, as well as build-to-suit options.
NIS is also preparing to launch its commercial hub in the fourth quarter of 2026, further expanding the facilities available to businesses operating within the industrial park.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Penang schools to operate as usual on Thursday despite haze
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: All educational institutions in the state will operate as usual tomorrow despite the haze affecting the country.
The Penang Education Department said it would continue monitoring air quality and prioritise the safety, health and well-being of students and education personnel.
"We remain concerned about the safety and health of students amid the deteriorating air quality," it said in a statement.
The department said students attending school are encouraged to wear face masks as a precaution and drink sufficient water to stay hydrated.
It said schools must also ensure an adequate supply of drinking water is available for students and staff.
Parents or guardians concerned about their children's health due to the haze may consider keeping them at home, provided they inform the school administration, it added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysian Bar, office-bearers awarded RM59,499 after winning part of appeal over 2022 independence march
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 21 —The Court of Appeal today partly allowed the Malaysian Bar’s appeal over its 2022 Walk for Judicial Independence, awarding RM59,499 in damages to the Bar and four of its office-bearers for violating their constitutional rights in connection with the march.
A three-member panel led by Justice Datuk Dr Choo Kah Sing ordered the government to pay RM19,499 in special damages to the Bar and RM10,000 each to Karen Cheah Yee Lynn, Mohamad Ezri Abdul Wahab, B. Anand Raj and Murshidah Mustafa, all office-bearers of the Bar when the suit was filed.
The march was held on June 17, 2022, to protest the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission’s (MACC) public announcement of an investigation into then Court of Appeal judge Datuk Mohd Nazlan Mohd Ghazali, now a Federal Court judge.
The Bar regarded the announcement as interference with judicial independence and a breach of the separation of powers.
On March 20 last year, the Kuala Lumpur High Court held that the police had acted
ultra vires
(beyond their powers) by imposing conditions prohibiting the march, but awarded the Bar only RM1 in nominal damages, a sum proposed by the Bar’s counsel.
The suit was filed on Oct 20, 2022, against six defendants, including former Dang Wangi police chief ACP Noor Dellhan Yahaya, the Inspector-General of Police, the Home Minister and the government, over alleged violations of the plaintiffs’ rights under the Peaceful Assembly Act 2012.
The plaintiffs claimed they were prevented from marching with about 500 members and interns from Padang Merbok to Parliament to submit a memorandum to then prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob or his representative.
Delivering the judgment, Justice Choo, sitting with Justice Datuk Faizah Jamaludin and Justice Datuk Dr Lim Hock Leng, also set aside the High Court’s finding that Kuala Lumpur City Hall’s (DBKL) consent was required for the assembly at Padang Merbok.
The court held that the Bar’s notification to police under Section 9 of the Peaceful Assembly Act 2012 was valid.
“A letter from the Dang Wangi district police chief imposing conditions on the march had been issued out of time and was invalid.
“The Bar had notified police on June 3, 2022, but received the response only on June 16, less than 24 hours before the assembly. Under Section 14 of the Act, police must respond with any conditions within three days,” he said.
However, the bench upheld the High Court’s dismissal of the false imprisonment claim, finding that the participants had not been totally deprived of their liberty.
“While participants were prohibited from marching to Parliament House, they were not physically restrained from leaving the area,” Justice Choo said.
The court also upheld the finding that the police were not liable for misfeasance in public office and dismissed the claim for misconduct in public office, as it failed to meet the high subjective threshold required.
The bench further declined to award general, aggravated and exemplary damages. It ordered interest at five per cent per annum on the sums awarded, from the date of the High Court’s judgment until full settlement, with no order as to costs.
The plaintiffs had sought special damages amounting to RM19,449, general damages and aggravated and exemplary costs, in addition to a declaration that their rights had been violated and a declaration that their detention was illegal and wrongful in law. — Bernama

Title: PM Anwar expresses concern over Middle East conflict, condemns Houthi attacks
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Malaysia continues to view with great concern the dangerous escalation of conflict unfolding across the Middle East, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Anwar said that he has been in close contact with key regional leaders, including Saudi Arabia’s Crown Prince Mohammed Salman and Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed Abdulrahman Al Thani.
According to him, these high-level discussions reflect the utmost gravity with which Malaysia regards the crisis and the urgent need to prevent it from widening further.
“Malaysia’s position is clear as we remain steadfast in our call for peace and justice for the Palestinian people, our unequivocal condemnation of the genocide in Gaza and our opposition to the indiscriminate bombing of southern Lebanon,” he said in a post on X today.
He emphasised that this same moral conviction compels Malaysia to speak out with equal firmness whenever innocent civilians are targeted anywhere else.
Consequently, Malaysia reiterates its strong condemnation of attacks by the Houthi movement against civilians and critical civilian infrastructure, such as airports and energy installations in Saudi Arabia and other Gulf Cooperation Council states.
He noted that the recent strike on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, which tragically claimed the lives of innocent civilians, including pilgrims, served as a sobering reminder of the devastating human toll of such violence.
The Prime Minister clarified that Malaysia’s firm stance targets those responsible for the aggression rather than the resilient people of Yemen, who have suffered years of hardship and deserve a lasting political settlement.
Furthermore, he stressed that maintaining the security of the Middle East’s vital sea lanes is paramount for a trading nation like Malaysia.
“Malaysia will continue to support all diplomatic efforts to de-escalate the crisis and safeguard the freedom of navigation,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Johari: Malaysia’s chip talent retention remains sustainable despite foreign offers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Starting salaries for junior engineers and technicians in the local chip industry scale up steadily with experience, offering sustainable career progression even as overseas markets tempt local talent with higher pay, said Minister of Investment, Trade and Industry Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani today.
Addressing questions in Parliament on wage competitiveness and talent retention, Johari said entry-level salaries for junior engineers typically start around RM3,500 and can reach RM6,000 as they gain experience, while technicians can earn between RM3,000 and RM5,000 depending on tenure.
Johari acknowledged the salaries may seem nominally low when compared to what companies in countries like Taiwan or South Korea may offer, but said they must still weigh higher overseas pay against the increased cost of living in those countries.
“If compared with job offers overseas in places like the UK, Singapore, Korea, or Taiwan, salaries might be two to three times higher,” Johari said during Question Time.
“However, the cost of living in those countries will also increase accordingly.”
The Anwar administration is actively trying to position Malaysia as a key chip player by the next one or two decades, rolling out policies it said would help push the domestic semiconductor ecosystem up the value chain.
Southeast Asia’s fourth-largest economy by GDP holds a crucial role in the global transistor supply chain, but only for back-end testing and assembly. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had said he wants Malaysia to shift into front-end design and wafer fabrication.
Retaining skilled human capital through progressive local wage structures remains central to driving the nation’s advanced technology ambitions, but compensation in Malaysia’s industrial sector must be viewed within the context of the domestic standard of living, Johari said.
Still, local pay structures could expand significantly for specialised roles as experience grows, the minister added.

Title: Loke envisions Transport Expo Asia rivalling LIMA as regional mobility showcase
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Transport Minister Anthony Loke hopes the biennial Transport Expo Asia (TXA) will develop into a premier international showcase on par with the Langkawi International Maritime and Aerospace Exhibition (LIMA), drawing top global exhibitors and industry investors to Malaysia.
Loke said that the event serves as an ideal launchpad to spotlight progress across land transport, aviation, maritime, and logistics sectors, placing particular emphasis on emerging technologies like autonomous driving, robotics, and unmanned aerial systems.
“We want TXA to establish its own brand, much like LIMA, which has become synonymous with Malaysia’s defence industry,” he said during a press conference after witnessing the exchange of memoranda of understanding (MoUs) and bilateral cooperation documents in conjunction with TXA 2026.
Loke pointed out that LIMA, established in the early 1990s, built a formidable global reputation over decades by convening aerospace and maritime manufacturers from around the globe.
He expressed confidence that TXA can chart an identical growth path, anticipating even stronger corporate participation when the exhibition returns for its third edition in 2028.
The trade event has already gained solid traction, recording nearly 5,000 visitors on its opening day yesterday, according to Loke.
The exhibition floor also served as a catalyst for dealmaking, facilitating the formalisation of 17 cooperation pacts aimed at driving sectoral expansion and technology transfer.
“This is something we encourage through Transport Expo Asia, as it provides a platform for industry players to establish strategic partnerships and use the opportunity to formalise their agreements or MoUs.
“We certainly hope this will help drive growth in the transport sector through greater strategic cooperation,” he said.
Rail modernization formed the centrepiece of the commercial exchanges, accounting for 13 of the 17 signed documents, while the remaining four addressed road mobility and maritime operations.
The multilateral pacts bring together government agencies, local operators, tertiary institutions, and overseas strategic partners, advancing Putrajaya’s broader infrastructural modernisation objectives outlined in the National Transport Policy 2030.
Loke said that the Transport Ministry is actively nudging corporations to deepen collaborative research and development with domestic public universities to accelerate the commercial deployment of homegrown inventions.
He cited university-designed vehicular and road safety innovations as tangible proof of how academic-industry links solve real-world mobility challenges.
To nurture youth talent, the exhibition also highlighted tertiary-level innovation initiatives, including a road safety challenge organised in collaboration with energy firm Shell that task university students with creating deployable crash-prevention solutions.
First established in 2025 as the Transport Ministry’s flagship international mobility and logistics exposition, TXA convenes policymakers, venture capitalists, engineering suppliers, and tech developers under one roof. The current three-day showcase runs through Oct 22.

Title: Sarawak completes integrated rare earth elements roadmap to build ‘super magnet’ industry, says Awang Tengah
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 21 — The Sarawak government has completed an integrated framework for the development of the rare earth elements (REE) industry, covering the entire value chain from upstream to downstream activities, said Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Awang Tengah Ali Hasan.
The Second Natural Resources and Urban Development Minister said the Sarawak REE Industry Development Roadmap aims to develop a ‘super magnet’ industry to support the growth of Sarawak’s semiconductor, aerospace, and satellite industries, in addition to applications in electric vehicle manufacturing, defence technology, medicine, and other sectors.
“As an initial step towards developing the industry, the Sarawak government has approved an allocation of RM18 million under the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP) to conduct studies on the potential presence of REE resources across an area of approximately 3,134 square km.
“In this regard, the federal government has been requested to provide a larger allocation to the Sarawak branch of the Department of Minerals and Geoscience Malaysia to enable the surveys on the presence of these mineral resources to be expanded throughout Sarawak,” he said when winding up his ministerial speech at the State Legislative Assembly (DUN) here.
On a related matter, Awang Tengah said the Sarawak Minerals Management Authority (SMMA) has approved the Sarawak Mineral Industry Development Policy, which comprises seven pillars and 43 key components.
“The policy emphasises the implementation of green mining and quarrying, the use of the latest technologies, human capital development, and the integrated development of the industry across the upstream, midstream, and downstream sectors to increase the value added of products,” he said.
He added that the Green Mining and Quarrying Academy, established through a strategic collaboration between the Centre for Technology Excellence Sarawak and the University of British Columbia (UBC), Canada, will serve as a platform to support the implementation of this policy. — The Borneo Post

Title: KLIA deploys K9 sniffer dog units to tighten airport security and curb smuggling
Article:
SEPANG, Oct 21 — Trained sniffer dog units will begin patrolling passenger terminals and restricted baggage zones across KL International Airport (KLIA) from Oct 26, Malaysia Airports announced today.
The units form a cornerstone of 17 enhanced security measures designed to thwart illicit smuggling and shore up national gateways. The K9 sweeps will operate across three critical operational sectors: the Departure Hall, the Arrival Hall, and the subterranean baggage sorting facilities.
The airport operator described the deployment as a multi-layered security strategy that shields public passenger-facing concourses while reinforcing back-of-house operations alongside existing surveillance architecture.
At check-in and departure gates, the canines will assist handlers in sniffing out prohibited substances and identifying security threats tied to high-risk flight profiles. In Customs inspection corridors, the dogs will intercept undeclared contraband, narcotics, and smuggled commercial goods.
Down in the baggage sortation areas, K9 units will inspect checked luggage before ramp crews load bags onto departing aircraft or transfer incoming cargo to passenger reclaim belts. To maintain animal welfare between rigorous operational shifts, dedicated rest stations and handler amenities have been designated across both terminals.
Malaysia Airports managing director Datuk Mohd Izani Ghani said integrating canine units into daily operations strengthens inter-agency vigilance to safeguard international travellers, visitors, and airport staff, while freeing airport Aviation Security (AVSEC) teams to concentrate on their primary protective functions.
“This collaboration also allows our Aviation Security personnel to remain focused on their core responsibility of safeguarding airport users and facilities.
“We will continue to support the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency, the Royal Malaysia Police, Royal Malaysian Customs Department and the K9 units in ensuring that KLIA remains a safe, comfortable and clean airport for everyone,” Mohd Izani said.
An initial pilot phase will fine-tune terminal standard operating procedures, secure restricted-area access protocols for handlers and dogs, and adjust patrol intervals to prevent disruptions to peak passenger movements.
The enhanced security perimeter arrives amid intense public scrutiny following several brazen narcotics trafficking cases traced back to Malaysian departure gates in recent months, though Malaysia Airports did not tie the canine rollout to any specific incident.
The deployment follows recent drug arrests abroad involving Malaysians said to have departed from KLIA.
On Oct 10, Japanese customs enforcement detained five young Malaysians aged 19 to 26 upon their arrival at Tokyo's Haneda International Airport after officers discovered five kilograms of cocaine hidden inside the hollowed-out soles of their platform shoes. Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan confirmed on Oct 16 that the syndicate couriers, including a married couple travelling under the guise of tourists without prior criminal records, boarded their flight from KLIA Terminal 2.
The Haneda seizure followed an earlier scandal in July, when a 39-year-old Malaysian commercial airline pilot was intercepted at Terminal 3 of Soekarno-Hatta International Airport in Jakarta in possession of 25 kilograms of ecstasy and methamphetamine pills valued at an estimated RM45 million.

Title: No more ‘kindergarten colours’: DBKL opts for neutral tones in RM446m public housing facelift
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — The capital’s public housing schemes are receiving a major aesthetic and safety facelift, with City Hall (DBKL) foregoing garish paint schemes for neutral tones while overhauling critical electrical infrastructure across dozens of ageing buildings.
Speaking during a working visit to People’s Housing Programme (PPR) Taman Mulia in Bandar Tun Razak today, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said that DBKL made a deliberate shift away from the bright, multi-coloured exteriors long associated with government flats.
Accompanying her on the site inspection were Kuala Lumpur Mayor Datuk Seri Fadlun Mak Ujud and Bandar Tun Razak MP Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail.
