“I would like to add that the colours chosen by DBKL are neutral colours, for the residents to know that this is a residential area and not a kindergarten.
“Many PPRs have been colourful, so we have chosen neutral colours,” she said.
Aside from the cosmetic exterior refresh, Yeoh said that the priority remains addressing life-threatening structural risks.
DBKL partnered with the Institution of Engineers Malaysia to conduct comprehensive technical audits across public housing schemes and municipal flats citywide, targeting deteriorating electrical risers and wiring to avert catastrophic fire hazards.
At PPR Taman Mulia, DBKL committed RM6.67 million in restorative works for roughly 2,128 residents. The project includes RM3.48 million towards repainting the towers, RM2.55 million to replace sub-main cabling and main switchboards, RM370,000 for internal road resurfacing, and RM272,000 to modernize fire prevention systems.
Mayor Fadlun said the citywide rehabilitation drive is moving steadily, with around 70 per cent of targeted projects completed. DBKL set 64 public housing sites for refurbishment in 2026, aiming to cross the 80 per cent completion line before year-end.
“The rest has been allocated for the 2027 budget, which we will continue for the PPRs and PAs that are not ready,” he said.
Fadlun further noted that Putrajaya has earmarked RM446 million in total for upgrading works across public housing estates and municipal flats, tailoring allocations to the specific infrastructural deficits of each scheme.
To ensure financial governance, DBKL plans to erect transparency signboards at individual housing estates displaying line-item expenditure, giving residents a clear accounting of public funds spent on their blocks.
Dr Wan Azizah reminded the community that structural improvements require civic responsibility, urging residents to safeguard shared amenities and combat vandalism.
“I see improvements, mainly in the PPRs area. However, what I would like to suggest is to take care of the infrastructure,” she said, noting that upkeep is indispensable if families are to enjoy secure and dignified living quarters.
Built in 2002, PPR Taman Mulia houses 912 residential units across two 21-storey towers. Having clocked more than two decades of heavy wear and tear, key mechanical and electrical fixtures required substantial rehabilitation to maintain habitability standards.
The estate was handed over to its Joint Management Body (JMB) on Dec 1, 2025, alongside a professional management agent to handle day-to-day estate administration.
DBKL reiterated that preserving public housing standards depends on continuous cooperation between the municipality, building managers, and resident committees.

Title: Malaysians who lend MyKad to foreigners face up to three years’ jail, says Home Ministry
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Individuals who misuse their identity cards (MyKad) by ‘renting out’ or handing them over to foreign nationals could face up to three years in prison, a fine of up to RM20,000, or both, Deputy Home Minister Datuk Seri Dr Shamsul Anuar Nasarah said.
He said the National Registration Regulations 1990 provide strict legal measures to curb foreign nationals’ misuse of national identity.
“The government takes this matter seriously, with enforcement aimed not only at penalising offenders but also at preventing identity misuse and identifying such cases at an early stage,” he said during a question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He was replying to a supplementary question from Mohamad Shafizan Kepli (GPS-Batang Lupar) about reports of some Malaysians renting out their MyKad to foreign nationals for only RM100 to work in factories.
Mohamad Shafizan had earlier highlighted the detention of 36 foreign factory workers in Pasir Gudang during Ops Jejak 1.0 yesterday for allegedly using fake MyKad or those belonging to other people to gain employment.
Shamsul Anuar said the operation underscored the importance of joint enforcement efforts by the National Registration Department (NRD), the Immigration Department and Labour Department.
“The operation also focused on the possible involvement of original identity card holders suspected of renting out or handing over their documents to foreign nationals for employment purposes,” he said.
On enforcement efforts, he said the NRD had carried out 4,174 operations nationwide from 2022 to September this year, resulting in 1,868 arrests.
He said 577 cases were prosecuted under Regulation 25(1)(e) of the National Registration Regulations 1990 during the same period, comprising 449 cases involving the use of fake MyKad and 128 involving the use of others’ identity cards. — Bernama

Title: Teacher injured while disarming student in Kuching school
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 21 — A teacher was injured while attempting to wrest a sharp object from a student at an international school here this morning.
It is learned that the secondary school student was brought under control and taken to the principal’s office before the police arrived and took over the matter.
The teacher was taken to the hospital for treatment.
Kuching district police chief ACP Alexson Naga Chabu, when contacted, said the police are looking into the incident.
There was no immediate information on what further action was taken on the student.
Efforts to contact the school for comments were unsuccessful.
An email purportedly sent by the school to its staff and parents of students, said the incident was isolated and no other injuries were reported.
It also said the students of the school were not in danger throughout the incident as they had been promptly moved to safety as precaution.
Lessons were ended early to allow police investigations. — The Borneo Post

Title: Find another way: Civil servants effectively banned from using Waze app due to Israel ties
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Civil servants have been banned from using the Waze navigation app with immediate effect, following a decision by the National Cyber Security Committee (JKSN) at its meeting yesterday.
In a letter dated October 20, Chief Secretary to the Government (KSN) Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar said the JKSN Meeting No. 3 of 2026 was chaired by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Shamsul Azri said all secretaries-general and department heads must ensure the decision is communicated to officers under their supervision, including related agencies and departments, for immediate implementation.
“Any queries or requests for further clarification regarding this directive may be submitted to the National Cyber Security Agency (NACSA), National Security Council, Prime Minister’s Department, as the coordinating agency for this matter,” the letter read.
He also sought cooperation and serious attention to ensure the decision is fully complied with at the ministry, department and agency levels.
The letter was addressed to all ministry secretaries-general, heads of federal departments, heads of management of federal statutory bodies, state government secretaries and heads of management of local authorities.
Yesterday, the Prime Minister encouraged the public to use the local TuJu app, developed by the Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM), as an alternative for road navigation.
Anwar said the recommendation followed security risks to users’ information and movement data from using Waze, which is bound under Israeli government laws.
TuJu was developed by LLM in collaboration with Prosignal Consortium Sdn Bhd and launched by Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi on Nov 26, 2025.
The app, available on the Google Play Store and Apple App Store, provides route information, travel distance, estimated time of arrival (ETA), toll and real-time traffic information, as well as rest and service area (R&R) facilities, live CCTV access and emergency assistance. — Bernama

Title: Hadi: PAS, aligned Perikatan parties to take joint action over RoS notice
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — PAS will join aligned Perikatan Nasional (PN) component parties in challenging a notice to cancel the coalition’s registration in court and preparing for the Melaka state election.
In a statement posted on Facebook today, PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang said the party condemned the move, which was communicated through a notice from the Registrar of Societies Malaysia (ROS) dated October 20.
PAS said the decision appeared to pre-empt a court ruling and restrict democratic rights guaranteed under the Federal Constitution.
The party also claimed the move reflected growing fear on the government’s part.
PAS maintained that PN’s administration and management had been conducted in an orderly manner and in accordance with the coalition’s constitution.
It said relations among PN’s component parties remained strong, except for one party which it claimed had distanced itself from the coalition and turned away.
Abdul Hadi said subsequent steps, including preparations for the Melaka state election and legal action to challenge the decision, would be taken jointly with PN component parties that remained aligned with the coalition.
PAS also thanked its members, supporters and fence-sitting voters who hoped for a change in the country’s leadership.
The party urged all parties to respect the law and democratic principles.

Title: Toll concessionaire ALR clears RM2.1b in debt, eyes early highway handover to Putrajaya
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Amanat Lebuhraya Rakyat Berhad (ALR) has crossed the RM2 billion threshold in cumulative sukuk principal and profit repayments, positioning the private not-for-profit firm to return four major Klang Valley toll highways to the government by 2033, five years ahead of schedule.
The milestone validates ALR’s enterprise model of using surplus toll collection solely to extinguish acquisition debt without paying dividends to shareholders, clearing the path for the state to take back the Kesas Expressway, Lebuhraya Damansara-Puchong (LITRAK), Western Kuala Lumpur Traffic Dispersal Scheme (SPRINT), and the Stormwater Management and Road Tunnel (SMART).
“On October 13, 2026, ALR made its eight sukuk payment of RM513.8 million comprising RM390 million to Sukuk Principal and RM123.8 million to Sukuk Profit, bringing its cumulative Sukuk Principal and Profit payments to more than RM2.149 billion.
“The Sustainability Sukuk Murabahah Programme carries total sukuk principal and profit obligations of RM7.935 billion,” ALR group chief executive officer Muhammad Nizam Alias told a media briefing at the SMART headquarters here today.
The latest debt servicing payment follows an earlier benchmark in April 2025, when cumulative payments touched RM1.021 billion.
“Surpassing RM2 billion in cumulative sukuk payments represents an important milestone in ALR’s journey.
“It demonstrates our continued financial discipline and commitment to meeting our obligations while remaining focused on the mandate entrusted to us to maintain toll affordability, eliminate the need for government compensation payments and accelerate the return of the highways to the government and the rakyat,” Muhammad Nizam said.
He explained that because ALR distributes no dividends, all net operational income flows directly toward servicing liabilities and sustaining day-to-day asset management.
Amanat Lebuhraya Rakyat Bhd group chief executive officer Muhammad Nizam Alias speaks during a press conference at the SMART Tunnel in Kuala Lumpur on October 21, 2026. — Picture by Firdaus Latif
“The milestone reflects the progress ALR has made since the issuance of the Sustainability Sukuk Murabahah in October 2022 and reinforces the connection between the group’s financial discipline and its long-term public-interest mandate.
“ALR issued RM5.5 billion in nominal value of AAA-rated Senior Sustainable and Responsible Investment Sukuk Murabahah on October 13, 2022 to finance the acquisition of four major urban highway concessionaires — KESAS, LITRAK, SPRINT and SMART.
“The acquisition was undertaken without the use of public funds or a government guarantee,” he said.
Established strictly as a transitional custodial entity, ALR freezes toll charges at existing gazetted levels throughout the tenure rather than imposing contractual hikes that require federal compensation payouts.
“Under its model, toll rates will remain at current levels until the respective concessions end, while surplus revenue is channelled towards the early redemption of debt financing,” he said.
Strong commuter traffic across the four networks has bolstered debt redemption timelines, setting up a potential full settlement well before the paper’s final maturity date in 2038.
“Under the sukuk programme, the longest maturity is 15 years, ending in 2038.
“However, based on our projections, the surplus accumulated each year could be sufficient by 2033 to settle the remaining sukuk obligations in a lump sum.
“The sooner we settle the entire sukuk amount, the sooner we can return the highways to the government.
“The government can then decide what to do with the highways, whether to charge nominal toll rates or make them toll-free.”
Alongside its role as a key bypass artery easing gridlock between Kuala Lumpur and the southern corridor, the dual-purpose SMART Tunnel plays a vital flood mitigation function for the city centre.
Since commencing operations in May 2007, the subterranean tunnel has diverted 266.03 million cubic metres of deluge over 685 flood-activation events, preventing an estimated RM4.94 billion in structural damage and public losses.
“Operating and maintaining critical infrastructure such as the SMART Tunnel required substantial financial resources.
“Nevertheless, it remained committed to its social responsibilities and continued to balance operational expenditure with toll revenue while meeting its sukuk obligations,” Muhammad Nizam said.
ALR maintains that its non-profit holding structure will continue to balance high engineering maintenance standards with steady debt retirement, ensuring motorists face no toll increases until the four concessions are formally returned to Putrajaya.

Title: Businessman charged with cheating Datuk Seri out of over RM10m in AMLA probe scam
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — A businessman was charged at the Sessions Court here today with four counts of cheating another businessman, who holds the title Datuk Seri, by claiming he could help resolve issues involving frozen bank accounts and a police investigation into more than RM10 million.
Tan Sri Tan Kean Soon, 63, however, pleaded not guilty to all four charges after they were read out before Judge Azrul Darus.
According to the charges, Tan allegedly cheated businessman Datuk Seri Keh Chuan Seng, 55, by deceiving him into believing that he could help resolve the freezing of Keh’s personal and company bank accounts by police, as well as a police investigation into Keh under the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001 (AMLA).
The deception allegedly induced Keh to hand over cash amounting to RM2 million, RM3 million, SGD1.5 million and RM500,000 to Tan through Datuk Seri Chiau Beng Teik, in which Keh would not have handed over the money had he not been deceived.
The offences were allegedly committed at a car park in Kuchai Lama, Dataran Maybank in Bangsar, Pavilion Hotel and Kampung Pandan here between March 23 and 25, 2025.
The charges were brought under Section 420 of the Penal Code, which provides for imprisonment of between one and 10 years, whipping and a fine upon conviction.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Norfauzani Mohd Nordin did not offer bail, citing the non-bailable nature of the offence and the total amount of money involved, which she said was RM10 million.
“If the court allows bail, the prosecution proposes RM2 million. However, he must notify the court and the prosecution of any overseas travel by letter and email,” she said.
Datuk Hisyam Teh Poh Teik, representing Tan, requested bail of RM1 million, saying his client needed to travel regularly to Singapore for medical treatment.
“My client is a businessman and has always cooperated fully with the police,” he said.
Bail was set at RM1 million with one surety, and Tan was ordered to inform the court and the prosecution of any overseas travel. Jan 11, 2027 was fixed for mention. — Bernama

Title: Ten former Negri exco members seek Federal Court interpretation of ruler’s powers
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 21 — Ten former Negeri Sembilan state executive council (exco) members have filed an application in the Federal Court seeking to challenge the state ruler’s decision last month to revoke their appointments.
The 10 are Datuk Mohd Faizal Ramli, Datuk Zaifulbahri Idris, Mustapha Nagoor, Siow Kong Choon, Siti Nur Umaira Hasim, Datuk Mohd Asna Amin, Datuk Mohd Razi Mohd Ali, Suhaimizan Bizar, Datuk Mohd Fairuz Mohd Isa and Datuk Razali Abu Samah.
They named the Negeri Sembilan state secretary and the state government as respondents.
They filed the notice of motion on October 14 this year through law firm Messrs Hafarizam Wan & Aisha Mubarak.
In the notice of motion, they want the Federal Court to determine three questions concerning the effect and interpretation of the provisions of the Negeri Sembilan State Constitution, which have arisen in their originating summons filed in the Seremban High Court.
On October 5 this year, they filed the originating summons to challenge the validity of a gazette revoking their appointments as exco members.
In their originating summons, they raised several constitutional questions.
Among the questions is whether Article 38(5), read together with Articles 38(2), 38(3), 38(4), 40(1), 40(1A) and 40(2) of the Negeri Sembilan Constitution, allows the Yang Dipertuan Besar to revoke the appointment of an exco without the Menteri Besar’s advice.
If the answer to that question is negative, whether the revocation of the exco members’ appointments, as gazetted on Sept 24 this year, was done in accordance with the Laws of the Constitution of Negeri Sembilan 1959 and therefore null, void and ineffective.
Another question is whether, under Article 38(5), read together with Article 28(1) of the Negeri Sembilan Constitution, the expression “Ruler” shall mean the Yang Dipertuan Besar alone at his pleasure can revoke the appointment of an exco without the advice of the Menteri Besar. If the answer to the above is in the negative, whether their dismissal is unconstitutional.
On September 20, the Negeri Sembilan palace announced that the Yang Dipertuan Besar, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, had revoked the appointments of the exco members with immediate effect.
The revocation of their appointments was gazetted on Sept 24, with their removal effective Sept 20.
The gazette stated that their appointments were revoked and annulled because they violated their pledge of allegiance to Tuanku Muhriz when they agreed on Tuanku Muhriz’s removal as the Yang Dipertuan Besar.
A case management is scheduled before the Federal Court Deputy Registrar today. — Bernama

Title: Sabah commercial vehicle body vows action against operator after deadly Sepanggar Port accident
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Oct 21 — The Commercial Vehicle Licensing Board (CVLB) Sabah will take action against the operator of the trailer truck involved in the fatal accident near Sepanggar Port on Sunday.
Chairman Datuk Phoong Jin Zhe said the board will meet on Oct 30 to discuss and finalise appropriate action against the operator.
He stressed that CVLB will not compromise on any negligence or breaches of regulations that could endanger road users.
This includes considering recommendations to suspend or revoke the relevant licence, subject to the findings of the investigation and applicable laws and regulations, he said.
He said CVLB Sabah will also continue to work closely with the Royal Malaysia Police and Road Transport Department (JPJ) to ensure that firm legal action is taken against those responsible.
In the incident on Sunday, a 53-year-old man and his 24-year-old daughter were killed when a container fell onto the car they were travelling in near Sepanggar Port.
Initial investigations found that the trailer had stopped on the left lane to load a container from the roadside onto the vehicle.
The container then fell onto a passing car.
It took firefighters more than three hours to extricate the victims from the wrecked car.
Both victims were pronounced dead at the scene by the paramedics and their bodies were later taken to Queen Elizabeth I Hospital for a post-mortem.
The 49-year-old trailer truck driver was detained by police to assist with investigations under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for causing the death of another person by driving a motor vehicle on a road recklessly or dangerously. — The Borneo Post

Title: High Court stays Malaysian Bar’s challenge against Zahid’s DNAA pending apex court appeal
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — The High Court has granted an interim stay on the Malaysian Bar’s judicial review challenging the Attorney General’s decision to halt corruption proceedings against Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
The decision freezes the challenge until the Federal Court disposes of the government’s appeal.
Justice Azizan Arshad granted the stay order in chambers today following an application by the Attorney General (AG), according to Zahid’s lawyer Guok Ngek Seong, FMT reported.
The freeze halts High Court proceedings after the Federal Court recently granted both the AG and the deputy prime minister leave to challenge an earlier Court of Appeal verdict that had permitted the Malaysian Bar to pursue its judicial review.
“The Federal Court has yet to fix a hearing date for the appeal as the notice of appeal was only filed on Oct 19,” Guok said.
Federal counsel Safiyyah Omar and Imtiyaz Wizni Aufa Othman appeared for the AG, while counsel S Abhilaash represented the Malaysian Bar.
Earlier this month, the apex court ruled that the AG and Zahid satisfied the statutory threshold under Section 96 of the Courts of Judicature Act 1964, clearing the way for full substantive arguments on whether prosecutorial discretion under Article 145(3) of the Federal Constitution is amenable to judicial review in such circumstances.
That decision paused the momentum generated by the Court of Appeal on May 7, when a three-judge panel unanimously overturned the High Court’s initial refusal to grant leave to the Bar.
The appellate court had reasoned that the Bar’s legal challenge was aimed directly at the “executive root”, namely the AG’s discretionary decision to discontinue the trial, rather than the criminal court’s subsequent judicial order granting Zahid a discharge not amounting to an acquittal (DNAA).
Zahid was granted a DNAA by the Kuala Lumpur High Court in September 2023 across all 47 criminal breach of trust, corruption, and money laundering charges involving millions of ringgit from charitable foundation Yayasan Akalbudi, after the prosecution applied to discontinue the case despite having established a prima facie case.

Title: Can the Yamtuan remove excos without MB’s advice? Sacked Negeri Sembilan councillors turn to apex court
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Ten dismissed Negeri Sembilan executive council members have mounted an unprecedented constitutional dispute at the Federal Court, asking it to determine if the Yang di-Pertuan Besar has the prerogative to revoke their appointments without the advice of the menteri besar.
The lawsuit challenges the decision by Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir to revoke their appointments, an order that took effect on Sept 20 and was formally gazetted on Sept 24.
The applicants comprise former councillors Faizal Ramli, Zaifulbahri Idris, Mustapha Nagoor, Siow Kong Choon, Siti Nur Umairah Hashim, Asna Amin, Razi Ali, Suhaimizan Bizar, Fairuz Isa, and Razali Abu Samah,
FMT
reported.
Through a notice of motion lodged on Oct 14, the group petitioned the apex court to rule on the constitutionality of their dismissal and declare the revocation null, void, and of no legal effect should it run counter to the state constitution.
The application names the Negeri Sembilan state secretary and the state government as the first and second respondents respectively.
Central to the dispute is the scope of royal discretionary powers. The applicants are seeking judicial determination on whether the phrase “at the ruler’s pleasure” in the state charter confers unbridled authority on the sovereign to dismiss executive councillors at will, irrespective of constitutional provisions requiring royal assent to align with the advice of the head of government.
Tuanku Muhriz previously stripped all ten executive council members of their posts for conduct the palace deemed treasonous to their oaths of office.
The palace acted after the councillors publicly endorsed a controversial declaration asserting that Tuanku Muhriz was legitimately dethroned in April and proclaiming Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja’afar as the state's rightful ruler.
The royal household held that backing a rival claimant to the throne was wholly incompatible with their sworn constitutional duty of allegiance to the reigning sovereign.

Title: Telcos set for bigger say as DNB ownership transition nears
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Malaysia’s major telcos are set to gain a bigger say over Digital Nasional Bhd’s direction as the wholesale 5G operator moves closer to a new ownership structure led by CelcomDigi, Maxis and YTL Power.
The transition follows DNB’s completion of a RM5.2 billion financing exercise, paving the way for the Ministry of Finance Inc (MOF Inc) to exit as an ordinary shareholder.
CelcomDigi, Maxis and YTL are expected to hold equal stakes in DNB, while MOF Inc will retain a special share covering key strategic matters. The transition is reportedly expected to be completed in early Q4 2026.
The change will give the mobile-network operators a larger role in steering DNB at a time when the telecommunications sector is under growing pressure to improve costs and network efficiency.
CGS International Research said earlier this month that once the share transfer is completed, the shareholders would be able to streamline DNB’s operations to minimise losses and improve the efficiency of the 5G rollout.
BIMB Research also recently said Malaysia’s telecommunications sector was increasingly shifting towards cost optimisation and disciplined execution as growth in the consumer segment remained modest.
Analyst Jamil Ghani, a PhD student at S Rajaratnam School for International Studies, said this could gradually change how DNB weighs its commercial and technology decisions.
“Future technology decisions are more likely to be driven by cost, performance, contract renewals, enterprise demand, interoperability, regulatory requirements and the transition towards 5G-Advanced and eventually 6G.”
However, he said it remained unclear whether the change would translate into any immediate shift in DNB’s technology suppliers.
“Ericsson’s 10-year partnership with DNB began in 2021,” he said, noting that it leaves roughly five years of existing commitments that would still have to be factored into future decisions.
DNB’s next move
DNB is now moving into a new phase focused on driving greater 5G adoption among businesses and industries.
Speaking on Oct 19, communications minister Fahmi Fadzil urged DNB to step up efforts to promote its 5G infrastructure to multinational companies, particularly secure and reliable connectivity solutions amid growing geopolitical uncertainty.
He also said that the government no longer held any financial obligations to DNB and has ruled out further state support.
DNB chief executive Azman Ismail said the company would work with its mobile-network operator shareholders, customers and technology partners to bring more practical 5G applications to market, including in manufacturing, logistics, healthcare, education, agriculture and smart cities.
He said high-quality and resilient connectivity would become increasingly important as businesses adopt more data-intensive and AI-powered applications at scale.
DNB was initially set up in 2021 as a wholly government-owned vehicle to build and operate Malaysia’s 5G network.
The government then announced a shift to a dual-network model in 2023. U Mobile was selected to build the second network, using China’s Huawei and ZTE technology.
MOF originally held a 35 per cent share in DNB. By Aug 2025, MOF Inc’s interest had risen to 41.67 per cent, while CelcomDigi, Maxis and YTL each held 19.44 per cent, following U Mobile’s exit from DNB’s shareholding. But in Dec 2025, MOF Inc subsequently exercised its put option, requiring CelcomDigi, Maxis and YTL Power to acquire its remaining equity and shareholder advances.

Title: Rapid KL trials fixed-schedule feeder vans in Cheras and Putrajaya, ditching app bookings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Commuters in parts of Cheras and Putrajaya will soon be able to board feeder vans on fixed timetables without booking via an app, as Rapid KL kicks off a three-month pilot project this Saturday, to boost first- and last-mile connectivity.
The trial shifts two existing Rapid KL On-Demand (ROD) zones, routes T400B and T512B, away from dynamic ride-hailing to predetermined routes and schedules. Dynamic on-demand bookings on both corridors will be temporarily halted during the testing window.
Route T400B bridges Bandar Tun Razak and Taman Midah, creating a direct ground link between the LRT Sri Petaling Line at Bandar Tun Razak station and the MRT Kajang Line at Taman Midah station.
In the administrative capital, Route T512B shuttles between Presint 11 and the Putrajaya Sentral transit hub, which feeds into the MRT Putrajaya Line and the KLIA Transit service.
Under the reworked model, passengers no longer need to book trips through the Rapid On-Demand mobile app. Instead, transit users can simply wait and board at designated stops along the loop, much like traditional feeder buses. Rapid KL has yet to release specific timetable intervals, frequencies, or operating hours for the trial vans.
Fares are set at a flat RM1 per trip throughout the three-month period. Passengers can pay via open payment contactless channels, including debit and credit cards, or standard Touch 'n Go cards.
Concession benefits remain intact, with MyRapid Concession Card holders eligible for a 50 per cent discount, while OKU riders holding the Rapid Mesra pass travel for free.
Rapid Bus Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Syahrul Azmir Ahmad Zaki said that the experiment is part of efforts to drive public transport adoption by lowering boarding friction.
“Rapid KL will also monitor usage, operational performance and user feedback to assess the public’s acceptance of and the effectiveness of this initiative.
“Findings gathered throughout its implementation will serve as a reference in considering service improvements in the future,” he said.
The transit operator plans to track daily passenger volumes, operational consistency, and user feedback over the 90-day trial to determine if the fixed-schedule van concept should be refined and deployed across other transit corridors.

Title: Loke: Prasarana open payment system procurement to be finalised by year-end
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Prasarana Malaysia Berhad is in the final stages of procuring a new open payment system that will allow commuters in the Klang Valley and Penang to pay for rail and bus fares using debit and credit cards, mobile wallets, and QR codes, Transport Minister Anthony Loke told Parliament today.
The initiative was first announced in 2023, and Loke at the time said a new payment system was needed to modernise fare collection across public transport networks operated by Rapid Rail and Rapid Bus by integrating more payment methods alongside existing options.
“This project is currently in the final stages of the procurement and evaluation process, with a decision expected to be finalised by the end of this year,” Loke replied to a query during Question Time.
“The implementation timeline is lengthy to ensure Prasarana’s full compliance with internal procurement standard operating procedures and guidelines, guaranteeing that the procurement process is conducted transparently.”
Once implemented, passengers will be able to pay using MyDebit cards, EMV-based international credit and debit cards, the minister said.
Payment service providers that could be employed would include Visa, Mastercard, American Express, UnionPay, and JCB, as well as contactless NFC devices and mobile wallets such as Apple Pay, Google Pay, Samsung Pay, and Alipay.
Loke said the new system will also support QR code ticketing, QR-based payments, Touch ‘n Go cards, and other future approved payment mediums.
The move came following years of calls for a better payment system as public transport users complained about the continued reliance on cash and a limited card-based payment through Touch ‘n Go, which they said causes unnecessarily long queues at the payment gates.
Some Opposition MPs had questioned why Prasarana still has adopted an open payment system, but Loke said the implementation process requires significant time to ensure full compliance with internal procurement standard operating procedures and governance guidelines.

Title: No order to step down: Shuhaily to remain on duty after claiming trial to assaulting Special Branch cops
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Malaysian Checkpoints and Borders Agency (MCBA) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain will remain at his post and carry out his duties as normal unless directed otherwise by the government, his legal team confirmed today.
Speaking to reporters outside the Sepang Sessions and Magistrates’ Court Complex, lawyer Datuk Rosal Azimin Ahmad said no official instructions or interdictions have been issued by administrative authorities barring his client from continuing as a senior civil servant.
Rosal clarified that any formal determination regarding Shuhaily’s service status rests entirely in the hands of the Public Service Department and central government leadership,
Berita Harian
reported.
“So far, in the absence of any directive, he will continue performing his duties as usual,” he said during a press conference following the morning court proceedings.
Touching on the bail hearing, Rosal revealed that the magistrate set bail at RM1,500 for each charge with one surety, amounting to a combined RM3,000.
The court fixed Nov 25 for next case mention. Rosal noted that the defence is awaiting the complete bundle of prosecution documents under Section 51A of the Criminal Procedure Code before deciding whether to submit formal representations to the Attorney-General’s Chambers.
Commenting on Shuhaily’s disposition, the lawyer said the 54-year-old enforcement chief remains calm and prepared to see the legal process through to its conclusion.
“He accepts what has happened and does not blame anyone,” he said.
Earlier in the morning, Shuhaily claimed trial to two counts under Section 323 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt to Lance Corporal Mohammad Faiz Muhamad Saman, 40, and Lance Corporal Muhammad Ekmal Sofwan Driman. If convicted, the minor assault charge carries a penalty of up to one year in prison, a maximum fine of RM2,000, or both.
The prosecution stems from a confrontation on Sept 28 at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Terminal 1, which drew intense public scrutiny after video footage went viral showing a senior official matching Shuhaily’s likeness rebuking two Special Branch travel control officers, with one of them appearing to be pulled by the ear.

Title: ‘If not us, who?’ — Nga Kor Ming hits back at critics of PM’s support for local artists
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming has defended Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim over his attendance at pop idol Datuk Seri Siti Nurhaliza's traditional concert last weekend, saying such patronage was vital to Malaysia’s creative industry.
Nga rejected criticisms over Anwar's presence at the weekend performance, stressing that government leadership must champion homegrown talent if the nation hopes to build a thriving arts ecosystem.
“When the government aims to develop the orange economy so local artists, painters, and musicians can earn a living, yet there are some who still object.
“So I want to ask: if the prime minister doesn't support local artists, then who will? If not us, who? And if not now, then when?” Nga told reporters after officiating the Toilet of the Year Award 2026 in Kuala Lumpur last night.
Drawing a sharp cultural comparison, the minister questioned the double standards often applied to local stars.
“If the United States can be proud of Taylor Swift, why can't we be proud of Siti Nurhaliza?” he said.
Nga disclosed that the Cabinet has agreed to establish a dedicated orange economy fund designed to empower the domestic music fraternity and nurture national creative talent.
He said state support must reach beyond individual headliners to encompass grassroots creative practitioners who elevate Malaysia's international profile, especially through cultural productions that showcase the country's diverse heritage on the world stage.
Yesterday, during Prime Minister’s Question Time in the Dewan Rakyat, Anwar addressed the issue directly, clarifying that he attended the massive concert at the Bukit Jalil National Stadium on Saturday upon a special invitation to celebrate traditional arts, heritage, and culture.
The prime minister noted that the showcase celebrated Malaysia's pluralistic cultural roots by incorporating traditional wayang kulit shadow puppetry, classical dance ensembles, and indigenous performances from Sabah and Sarawak, presenting the country's artistic heritage to an arena-sized modern audience.

Title: Perlis MB Abu Bakar stripped of party posts after Bersatu issues two-term suspension
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) has suspended Perlis Menteri Besar Abu Bakar Hamzah for two terms, effective Oct 13.
Perlis Bersatu state chairman Izizam Ibrahim confirmed the punitive action today, acknowledging that the formal notification letter was served on Abu Bakar last week after an internal disciplinary inquiry,
Berita Harian
reported.
The confirmation comes after a copy of the confidential dismissal notice surfaced online and circulated aggressively across social media channels over the past 48 hours. Izizam moved quickly to dismiss rumours that he leaked the document to the public.
“Yes, it is true that the letter was issued last week, but I was not the one who circulated it. The menteri besar is also already aware of the suspension letter.
“For now, we are waiting for an official decision from the Bersatu central leadership as well as the PAS state assemblymen,” he said.
The letter, dated Oct 14, 2026, was signed by Bersatu disciplinary board chairman Datuk Mohd Radzi Manan. The notice formally conveyed the board’s decision to penalise Abu Bakar, who also serves as the party’s Kangar division chief.
According to the document, the board convened on Oct 13 and invoked Clause 22.5 of the Bersatu Constitution to freeze Abu Bakar’s membership rights across two successive party election terms. The sanction followed findings that he had breached Clause 9.1.4 of the party constitution alongside the party’s statutory Code of Ethics and Conduct for Members.
With the disciplinary action in place, Abu Bakar has been immediately stripped of all internal party positions and barred from issuing public statements on behalf of Bersatu throughout his suspension.
The notice give the embattled menteri besar 14 days to contest the sanction and file a formal petition with the Bersatu appeals board.

Title: Floodwaters destroy Pos Brooke suspension bridge, leaving villagers isolated
Article:
GUA MUSANG, Oct 21 — A flash flood, accompanied by surging waters and a mudflow, caused the Kampung Brooke Lama suspension bridge across Sungai Belatop in Pos Brooke here to collapse yesterday afternoon.
The collapse cut off the main access route for more than 100 Temiar Orang Asli residents, disrupting daily activities, including getting their children to school and accessing healthcare.
Kampung Brooke Lama headman Rian Bujang said rain began at about 4 pm before the flash flood struck at around 5.30pm, sending strong currents crashing into the bridge, causing it to collapse and its concrete pillars to break.
“The situation was frightening as the strong, muddy currents overflowed onto the road and reached areas near residents’ houses,” he told Bernama today.
He said the bridge, built in 2008, served as an access route to Sekolah Kebangsaan Pos Brooke and Pos Brooke Health Clinic. Residents now have to use a longer alternative route via Kampung Liak and Kuala Rengil.
Meanwhile, Kelantan and Terengganu Department of Orang Asli Development (JAKOA) director Mohd Faedzyal Mohamed said about 44 families were affected and that the department had informed the Disaster Operations Control Centre to seek emergency assistance.
Some residents have taken shelter at the open hall of the JAKOA Pos Brooke office, while the bridge had previously drawn the attention of Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi in 2023 over safety concerns, with the South Kelantan Development Authority (Kesedar) and JAKOA instructed to undertake repairs or improvements. — Bernama

Title: MCBA chief Shuhaily charged with assaulting Special Branch duo at KLIA
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Malaysian Checkpoints and Borders Agency (MCBA) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain was charged at the Magistrate's Court here today to two counts of assaulting police personnel at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) last month.
Shuhaily claimed trial after both charges were read before Magistrate Khairatul Animah Jelani,
FMT
reported
He is accused of two counts under Section 323 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt to Lance Corporal Faiz Saman and Lance Corporal Ekmal Sofwan at KLIA Terminal 1 on Sept 28. Each charge carries a maximum penalty of one year's imprisonment, a fine of up to RM2,000, or both upon conviction.
Khairatul allowed Shuhaily bail of RM3,000 with two sureties across both charges, and fixed Nov 25 for case management.
Deputy public prosecutors Shahrizat Ismail and Sazali Omar prosecuted, while an eight-member defence team led by counsel Kitson Foong represented the border agency chief.
Speaking to reporters outside the courtroom before proceedings commenced, Shuhaily thanked supporters present at the court complex as well as those offering encouragement from afar.
“I will let due process take its course. And this will be my last press conference on this case,” he said.
The prosecution follows the viral spread of closed-circuit television (CCTV) recordings depicting an aggressive confrontation involving Shuhaily at the airport terminal.
MCBA subsequently authenticated the video, saying the altercation took place while the director-general was conducting an on-site operational inspection at KLIA ahead of the Bahrain Grand Prix events in Malaysia.
Shuhaily previously alleged that unnamed parties were orchestrating a campaign to tarnish his reputation and discredit the newly formed border agency, while maintaining that he would cooperate fully with investigators and accept the outcome of the legal process.

Title: Closing pig farms could weaken food security, says LDP leader
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Oct 21 — Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) vice-president David Ong has criticised a proposal to shut down pig farms nationwide and rely on imported pork, saying it could undermine Malaysia’s food security, local agriculture and multicultural values.
Ong was responding to a suggestion by Tasek Gelugor MP Wan Saiful Wan Jan, arguing that environmental and public health concerns should be addressed through better farm management, modern technology and stricter environmental standards rather than closing the industry.
He said food security required maintaining domestic production capacity to guard against supply disruptions, price fluctuations and changes in foreign export policies, adding that pig farming also supported farmers, workers, suppliers and other businesses along the supply chain.
Ong said policies must also respect Malaysia’s diverse communities and dietary practices, particularly in Sabah and Sarawak, while balancing environmental protection with agricultural development.
He urged political leaders to consider the economic and social consequences of their proposals, saying Malaysia should strengthen local food production and improve environmental standards rather than become unnecessarily dependent on imports. — Daily Express

Title: Guan Eng warns of SME liquidity crisis over RM30b delayed tax refunds
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Former finance minister Lim Guan Eng has urged the federal government to expedite the repayment of RM29.919 billion in tax refund arrears, warning that holding back businesses’ own money severely strains corporate liquidity, particularly among struggling small and medium enterprises (SMEs).
Lim, who is the member of parliament for Bagan, pointed to the 2025 Federal Government Financial Statements, which show that outstanding tax refund liabilities decreased by RM3.425 billion, dropping from RM33.342 billion in 2024 to RM29.919 billion in 2025.
While acknowledging the Inland Revenue Board (IRB) for whittling down the balance owed to firms that overpaid their taxes, Lim stressed that the outstanding sum remains colossal by any benchmark, especially since it belongs to the private sector.
“In 2026, RM9 billion was paid to 130,000 companies by Sept 30,” he noted, adding that the government must repay companies, especially the 1.2 million SMEs, more quickly.
To curb systemic delays, Lim proposed placing a strict RM10 billion cap on federal tax refund arrears. He argued that allowing the backlog to hover near RM30 billion inflicts undue financial hardship on cash-strapped businesses wrestling with deteriorating operating environments and a volatile global economic climate.
Historical data demonstrates a steady accumulation over recent years, Lim said. Outstanding tax refund commitments stood at RM21.836 billion in 2021, before climbing to RM25.721 billion in 2022 and RM25.511 billion in 2023.
The DAP lawmaker also took direct aim at public officials tasked with safeguarding small businesses, questioning why statutory agency leaders have failed to advocate forcefully for the immediate release of these funds.
“Failing to consistently and persistently press the government to return back to SMEs their own money, may give the unfortunate impression that those responsible and holding statutory positions are ‘sleeping on the job’.”
Lim also pointed out that statutory late-payment penalties have surged sharply as a consequence of refund delays. Under Section 111D of the Income Tax Act, the government is mandated to pay an annual 2 per cent compensation to taxpayers when IRB fails to disburse excess tax refunds within stipulated timeframes.
While IRB disbursed RM23.64 million under this mechanism in 2025, that penalty figure escalated by nearly fivefold in the first nine months of 2026 alone, hitting RM109 million as of Sept 30.

Title: Perak Perhilitan monitoring elephant herd after crop destruction complaints
Article:
IPOH, Oct 21 — The Perak Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) has received six official complaints this year from oil palm smallholders in Kampung Perlop 1, Sungai Siput, over wild elephants destroying crops and plantation infrastructure.
Its director, Dr Pazil Abdul Patah, said the herd is estimated at between three and eight elephants, believed to have come from the nearby Korbu Forest Reserve.
"The herd encroaching on Kampung Perlop 1 originally came from the Piah Forest Reserve in Lenggong, which has an estimated total of about 50 elephants, but has now split into smaller groups.
"Perhilitan also believes these are the same elephants that encroached into fruit orchards around Bukit Bangkong, Chemor, on Oct 15, as both locations fall within the range of the Korbu Forest Reserve," he said in a statement.
Yesterday, 18 oil palm smallholders appealed for urgent intervention from the authorities to tackle incursions by the mammals, which have destroyed crops spanning 80 hectares since early September.
Earlier, 12 farmers in Bukit Bangkong similarly appealed to the authorities for action to protect their 9.7-hectare fruit orchards from persistent elephant threats.
Meanwhile, Pazil said the department is actively monitoring the herd's movements to determine the most effective approach to resolve the conflict.
"For the long term, the department will focus on identifying conflict hotspots, strengthening early reporting systems, and expanding community awareness programmes," he said.
Pazil also advised affected smallholders to report incidents promptly to Perak Perhilitan so that applications under the Property and Crop Damage Assistance (BKHT) scheme can be processed in accordance with established requirements.
He said applicants should provide details including the plantation's location, the type and estimated cost of damage, the date of the incident, and supporting documents such as photographs and proof of land ownership or tenancy. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia calls for WHO-led pooled medicine purchasing amid supply risks
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Malaysia has proposed that the World Health Organisation (WHO) Western Pacific Region (WPRO) urgently pilot a pooled procurement project for selected medicines to ensure drug security in the region.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said the move was urgent as almost the entire region is facing critical challenges due to disrupted supply chains, market uncertainty, and high reliance on Active Pharmaceutical Ingredient (API) imports, with international geopolitical conflicts worsening the situation.
“Regional diplomacy and solidarity today must be translated beyond mere expressions of good intentions. To protect the survival of health systems in the Western Pacific, we demand a strategic, bold shift in action focused on tangible, measurable results,” he said in a Facebook post yesterday.
Dzulkefly presented the proposal at the Ministerial Roundtable held in conjunction with the 77th WHO WPRO Regional Committee Meeting.
He said the pooled procurement pilot project must involve selected medicines with healthy supplier competition and clear shared needs, and must be implemented transparently.
To support the mechanism, Dzulkefly proposed developing an ASEAN Medicines Security Dashboard as an early warning system linking pricing information with supply distribution, stock availability, and manufacturing capacity.
He also stressed that price monitoring alone could not absolutely guarantee medicine security.
Instead, he said the region needs a strategic manufacturing alliance through joint investment initiatives to cover production gaps.
“To realise this major framework, it requires clear leadership from a lead country under the 2026-2030 Plan, complete with funding accountability and clear key performance indicators,” he said.
Domestically, he said Malaysia has institutionalised pooled procurement across government health facilities, maintained a three-month medicine buffer stock, and spearheaded the ASEAN Drug Security and Self-Reliance (ADSSR) initiative.
He added that Malaysia would continue to leverage global health diplomacy platforms to ensure uninterrupted treatment for the people. — Bernama

Title: Corporate-creative collaborations vital to boost Malaysian IPs, says Teo
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Collaborations between corporate entities and local creative talent are vital in driving the growth of Malaysia’s creative sector and showcasing homegrown intellectual properties (IPs) to a broader audience.
Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said such strategic collaborations between corporate entities and homegrown creative teams allow local artists, animators, performers, and production personnel to showcase their skills on a wider stage.
“Usually, when we speak about local animation and creative content, we think of something we watch on television, in the cinema, or on our phones. Today, we get to walk into the story, meet its characters, and experience the world our own creators have imagined,” she said.
Speaking at The Haunted Highlands 2026 Press Conference and Exclusive Media Preview at Pavilion Hall, Skytropolis Indoor Theme Park here today, Teo praised Resorts World Genting for investing in Malaysian talent.
“For our creative industry to grow, we need businesses willing to believe in Malaysian talent and give Malaysian stories room to develop,” she said.
She explained that transforming animated IPs into physical attractions demonstrates how the creative and tourism sectors can mutually reinforce each other.
“An animated character that audiences first meet on screen can become part of a family’s holiday experience. Visitors may discover the attraction first, then go home and look up the series. That connection helps our creative industry and our tourism industry grow together,” Teo said.
Reiterating the government’s commitment to developing the nation’s Orange Economy, she outlined key allocations under Budget 2027 aimed at driving growth across the creative sector.
“These include allocating over RM130 million to support the creative industry, providing incentives for film and animation productions, exempting local film screenings and theatre performances in the Federal Territories from entertainment duty starting in 2027, and aiming to create 20 new animation intellectual properties (IPs),” she said.
Additionally, she pointed out that funding agencies such as MyCreative Ventures provide financial support through grants, loans, and equity investments across various creative pillars.
She added that eligible local animation film productions can also benefit from the National Film Development Corporation Malaysia’s (FINAS) Film in Malaysia Incentive (FIMI).
“Successful applicants may receive a 30 per cent cash rebate on qualifying Malaysian production expenditure (QMPE), with an additional rebate of up to five per cent for productions that meet the Malaysian Cultural Test, subject to the applicable terms and conditions,” she said. — Bernama
